note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Upper respiratory infection.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Andrew Campbell is a 59-year-old male who presents today with an upper respiratory infection. The patient reports that he was doing some yard work in the last week or so and started to feel really tired and short of breath. He believes that he caught his first cold in the last few weeks and that it has gotten worse. The patient reports that he has been wearing masks less frequently at the end of the summer. He denies any history of seasonal allergies.

The patient reports that he is currently doing well with his depression, but notes that it has been a crazy year and a half. He has been attending barre classes to help him relax. He notes that his diabetes has been well-managed while he is at work, but notes that he does not monitor his sugar levels on weekends. He notes that his blood pressure has been well-managed with home monitoring, but notes that he does not monitor it on weekends.

The patient denies any fevers, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or joint pain.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Reports fatigue.
• Respiratory: Reports shortness of breath.
• Musculoskeletal: Reports elbow pain and knee pain.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Cardiovascular: Regularly regular rate and rhythm. No murmurs, gallops or rubs heard.
Respiratory: Scattered ronchi bilaterally on auscultation of lungs. Clear to auscultation with cough.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Chest x-ray obtained today shows no airspace disease or pneumonia.
Hemoglobin A1c 8.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Upper respiratory infection.
• Medical Reasoning: This appears to be a viral syndrome based on the patient’s symptoms and examination findings today.
• Medical Treatment: We will send a COVID-19 test today to rule out COVID-19 exposure. I will prescribe Robitussin for cough and recommend ibuprofen or Tylenol for fever management.
• Patient Education/ Counseling: I advised the patient to continue home monitoring of blood pressure as well as home monitoring of blood glucose levels while at work during the week. We discussed the importance of attending barre classes for stress relief as well as continued home monitoring of blood pressure and blood glucose levels while at work during the week.
Type 2 diabetes mellitus.
• Medical Reasoning: His hemoglobin A1c was elevated at 8% today; however, this is within normal limits when compared to previous labs which were around 6-7%.
• Medical Treatment: I increased his metformin dosage to 1000 mg twice daily daily. We will follow up in 4 months for another hemoglobin A1c level.
High blood pressure.
• Medical Reasoning: His blood pressure was well-controlled with home monitoring during the week; however, this was not consistent on weekends due to social obligations such as house parties etc., which may have contributed to elevated readings on those days.
• Medical Treatment: Continue lisinopril 20 mg daily. Order lipid panel today.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Annual exam.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Andrea Roberts is a 52-year-old female with a past medical history significant for rheumatoid arthritis, atrial fibrillation, and reflux who presents today for her annual exam.

The patient reports that she has been walking and exercising as directed. She has not had any joint pain recently. She endorses palpitations but notes that they have improved with meditation and running with her dog. She denies any issues with stiffness or pain or flare-ups over the last year.

Regarding her atrial fibrillation, the patient reports that she has been experiencing palpitations. The last one was about a week ago. She notes that they start to flare up when she is stressed. She has been trying meditation and running with her dog to relieve stress but it has not helped.

She endorses nasal congestion due to allergies.

INDEPENDENT REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Cardiovascular: Endorses palpitations.
Respiratory: Endorses nasal congestion.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Cardiovascular: 2/6 systolic ejection murmur appreciated in the right upper quadrant of the chest. Regular rate and rhythm at this time.
Respiratory: Lungs are clear bilaterally.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Event monitor results show that you are in and out of atrial fibrillation, you have what we call a conversion pause. You are in atrial fibrillation, you pause, and then you go back to regular rhythm.
Autoimmune panel shows everything looks good. It looks like you are well controlled with your rheumatoid arthritis on methotrexate.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Annual exam.
- Rheumatoid arthritis: Normal autoimmune panel; Continue methotrexate 2.5 mg once weekly; Order methotrexate 2.5 mg once weekly refill as needed.
- Atrial fibrillation: Endorses palpitations; Recommend referral to cardiology for cardiac ablation; Order referral to cardiology today.
- Gastroesophageal reflux disease: Continue protonix 40 mg daily; Continue dietary modifications avoiding coffee and spicy foods; Order additional prescription refills as needed.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Emergency room follow-up.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Albert Powell is a 62-year-old male who presents today for emergency room follow-up. The patient was seen in the emergency room last week due to uncontrolled blood sugar levels. He was admitted to the hospital, but was discharged home after feeling better. The patient reports that he has been eating poorly since his mother had a hip replacement and has not been monitoring his diet. He denies chest pain or shortness of breath, but reports lightheadedness and dizziness.

The patient reports that he is doing well with his kidney transplant. He has been taking immunotherapy medications as prescribed and has been following doctor’s orders.

The patient reports that he has been doing well with his depression. He finds meditation relaxing and would like to continue this practice for another couple of months before considering medical therapy.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Reports lightheadedness and dizziness.
• Cardiovascular: Denies chest pain or shortness of breath.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Cardiovascular: Grade 2/6 systolic ejection murmur heard at the left lower sternal border.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Hemoglobin A1c: 8.
Fasting Glucose: 162.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Albert Powell is a 62-year-old male, with a past medical history significant for depression, type 2 diabetes, and kidney transplant, who is here today for emergency room follow-up.

Hyperglycemia.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient’s hemoglobin A1c was elevated at 8% and his fasting glucose was elevated at 162 mg/dL. This warrants an increase in insulin dosing to 20 units at night.
- Medical Treatment: I have increased his Lantus insulin to 20 units at night. We will monitor his blood sugars and adjust as needed.
- Patient Education/ Counseling: We discussed the importance of monitoring blood sugars and adjusting insulin dosing as needed based on results.
- Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan.

Depression.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient is doing well with meditation as a coping mechanism for depression. We will hold off on medical therapy or therapy at this time, but we will continue to monitor him closely if needed.
- Medical Treatment: No medical treatment recommended at this time. We will continue to monitor him closely if needed.
- Patient Education/ Counseling: We discussed the importance of continuing meditation as a coping mechanism for depression until we feel he is ready to try additional medical treatment options such as medication or therapy.
- Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan.

Kidney transplant.
- Medical Reasoning: His kidney function appears stable based on recent labs from Dr. Reyes’ office visit last week. I have recommended that he continue following up with Dr. Reyes regarding immunosuppression medications as needed.
- Medical Treatment: No additional medical treatment recommended at this time. We will continue to monitor him closely if needed.
- Patient Education/ Counseling: We discussed the importance of continuing immunosuppression medications as prescribed by Dr. Reyes’ office visit last week until we feel he is ready to discontinue them due to stable kidney function based on recent labs from Dr. Reyes’ office visit last week.
- Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Annual exam.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Jerry Nguyen is a 54-year-old male who presents for an annual exam. The patient reports that he has been traveling all over the country and adjusting to everything in the fall. He notes that he has been experiencing lack of sleep, which has been getting to him. The patient has tried melatonin, meditation, and t- stretching out every morning when he gets up, but nothing seems to help.

The patient reports that he is currently taking fosamax 1 tab per week for osteoporosis. He denies any issues with his joints or recent broken bones.

Regarding his multiple sclerosis, the patient last saw the neurologist 6 months ago. He is currently taking his medication without any issues. The patient denies any additional weakness.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Sleep: Insomnia.
• Constitutional: No chest pain or shortness of breath.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

• Neurological: Lax reflexes bilaterally. L4-L5 radicular pain in right lower extremity.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-ray of the right knee was obtained today and reviewed by me in office today. There are changes from arthritis.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Jerry Nguyen is a 54-year-old male with a past medical history significant for osteoporosis and multiple sclerosis who presents for an annual exam.

Osteoporosis: Continue fosamax 1 tab per week, 11 refills.
Multiple sclerosis: Continue current medications as prescribed and follow up with neurology as needed.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Right arm pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Amanda Martinez is a 43-year-old female who presents today for evaluation of right arm pain. The patient reports that she was playing tennis when she hit the top of the net with her arm. She denies any swelling or numbness in her hand. She takes Flonase for allergies.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports right arm pain.
Neurological: Denies numbness in her hand.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Musculoskeletal: Examination of the right upper extremity reveals tenderness over the distal radius.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

The patient is a 43-year-old female who presents today for evaluation of right arm pain. She reports that she was playing tennis when she hit the top of the net with her arm. She denies any swelling or numbness in her hand. She takes Flonase for allergies.

Examination of the right upper extremity reveals tenderness over the distal radius.

Medical Reasoning and Treatment Plan: I reviewed her x-ray today and there were no fractures or abnormalities noted. I believe this is likely a strain and contusion to the muscle from hitting it on the net. We will treat conservatively with ice, anti-inflammatory, and Motrin 800 mg three times a day with food. If it does not improve in 1 week, we will follow up again.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Back pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Cheryl Ramirez is a 34-year-old female with a past medical history significant for hypertension, who presents today with back pain. Cheryl reports that she has been walking a lot lately, 30 minutes to an hour or so a day. All of a sudden, she felt like her back just kind of seized up on her. She denies lower extremity numbness, tingling, and weakness. She endorses nasal congestion from seasonal allergies.

PAST HISTORY

Medical: Significant for hypertension.

SOCIAL HISTORY

Patient reports that she has been lifting more, probably around 3 times a week. She endorses that she was using her back more than her legs.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Constitutional: Reports nasal congestion from seasonal allergies.
Neurological: Denies lower extremity numbness, tingling, and weakness.
Musculoskeletal: Endorses back pain.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Cardiovascular: Grade 2/6 systolic ejection murmur stable to repeat examination.
Musculoskeletal: Examination of the lumbar spine reveals tenderness to palpation on the right lateral aspect of the lumbar spine. Pain with flexion and extension as well as negative straight leg raise.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Back x-ray obtained today. There is good bony alignment without evidence of fracture.
Labs were reviewed today and are all within normal limits.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Cheryl Ramirez is a 34-year-old female with a past medical history significant for hypertension who presents today with back pain.
- Medical Reasoning: I believe this is due to lumbar strain secondary to lifting or exercising.
- Medical Treatment Plan: I have prescribed meloxicam 15 mg once daily. She can ice the area and apply heat as well. We will refer her to physical therapy for strengthening exercises of her back because I want her to continue working out and exercising. We will follow up in 2 weeks at that time if there has been no improvement in symptoms.
- Patient Education and Counseling Plan: I advised the patient that she should continue taking lisinopril 10 mg daily as prescribed by me today. We discussed the importance of monitoring her blood pressure at home and reporting any increases in blood pressure readings to me at our next visit.
- Additional Testing or Referrals: No additional testing or referrals are needed at this time.

The patient is a 44-year-old female who presents today for evaluation of left shoulder pain.

- I advised her to avoid lifting heavy objects until her arm heals, which should be at least 3 weeks.
- She should follow up with me if her symptoms persist after 3 weeks.
- Additional x-rays may be needed if her symptoms do not improve after 3 weeks.

Patient Agreements:
She understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan.

Evaluation of illness.

His mother notes that he has been irritable and has not slept well. She notes that he had a fever this morning, but it has resolved. The patient ate about 7 ounces from the bottle this morning, but did not eat the cereal she offered him. His mother reports that he is using saline nasal spray in his nose and Tylenol for fever.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Fever.
• Respiratory: Runny nose, congestion, cough.
• Ear: Ear pain.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Ears: No discharge or erythema.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Randy Gutierrez is a 9-month-old male who presents today for evaluation of an upper respiratory infection.

Medical Reasoning:
- This appears to be a viral upper respiratory infection.
- Often sinus infections will start out as a virus and then will become bacterial infections if left alone and does not go away. However, I do not think he needs antibiotics at this point in time.
- Keep up with fluids, rest, and watch for a barking cough. If he develops one, give him half a teaspoon of his sister's medicine.
- Do not give honey to babies under 1 year old because it can cause botulism spores to grow in their stomach acid which can cause harm to them. Agave nectar is okay though.
- Use Zarbee's for the stuffy nose.
- Give him the same medicine as his sister if needed just hang onto it to watch and see if things get worse over the weekend. If they do worsen call us if needed. If they don't worsen just use it as needed for 5 days at half a teaspoon per dose for kids under 1 year old.
- Continue using the soft brush and baby oil twice weekly to help prevent cradle cap from coming back again within 6 weeks or so. Avoid rinsing his eyes when using these products as they are not ph balanced for eyes.
- If cradle cap gets worse contact us again.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Acne.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Kayla Ward is a 15-year-old female who presents today for a new visit with her mother for acne located on the face, which started about two years ago and is present most every day. She has been using Persa-Gel and washing regularly, which is somewhat helpful. There are no associated symptoms including itching, bleeding, or pain.

PAST HISTORY

Medical: No additional past medical history.

SOCIAL HISTORY

Lives with parents and sister. They have a dog, bird, and rabbits in the home. She is in 7th grade and active in basketball, volleyball, and tap dancing.

FAMILY HISTORY

No significant family medical history.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Skin: Reports acne on the face. Denies itching, bleeding, or pain.
Gynecologic: Reports regular periods.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
- Skin: Multiple benign nevi on the trunk and extremities. Scattered skin colored papules. Open and closed comedones. Erythmateous papules on the face, primarily on the forehead and with also some on the central cheeks and chin. The chest and back are relatively spared.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Kayla Ward is a 15-year-old female who presents today for a new visit with her mother for acne located on the face.
Mild to moderate acne, mostly comodonal with small inflammatory component.
Plan: Start with topical therapy first. Every morning she will wash her face with a mild cleanser then use a moisturizer labeled "noncomedogenic," with sunscreen SPF 30 or higher. This means it won't clog her pores. Now in the evening wash her face with the same cleanser and allow it to dry. Apply adapalene 0.1% cream in a thin layer to the areas she generally gets acne. I want her to start off using this a few nights per week and slowly work up to using it every night if it is very expensive or not covered by insurance she can try different gel over-the-counter products such as Clean & Clear Persa-Gel in a thin layer or where she generally gets acne followed by noncomedogenic moisturizer. She will need to wear sunscreen when she is outside due to atopic retinoid causing sensitivity which may cause some dryness or irritation.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Breast reduction.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Julia Jones is a 25-year-old female with symptomatic macromastia, presenting for evaluation of breast reduction. The patient has attempted nonsurgical treatments, but the minimal relief. She is an ideal candidate for bilateral reduction mammoplasty.

The patient reports that she has been considering a breast reduction for approximately six to seven years. She states that she has been going to the chiropractor for back pain for several years and that she believes this pain is related to her breasts. She reports that her bra strap indentations are in her shoulders and that she wears a g-cup bra. The patient denies any children and does not plan on having any in the future. She does report numbness and tingling in her hands and nipple pain. The patient also reports rashes underneath her breasts due to sweating.

The patient reports that she experiences back pain, neck pain, and shoulder pain. She attributes this to her breasts as it gets painful and builds up when working at her desk all day. The patient denies any numbness or tingling in the hands or nipple pain.

The patient denies any history of breast cancer in her family but notes that her mother was diagnosed with breast cancer at age 40. She states that she started mammograms at age 30 but is still a little bit young.

She denies tobacco use, alcohol use, or illicit drug use.

She is currently studying psychology.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Reports weight loss over the past few months.
• Musculoskeletal: Reports back pain, neck pain, shoulder pain.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

• Breast: Asymmetrical breasts with severe ptosis bilaterally.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Julia Jones is a 25-year-old female with symptomatic macromastia, presenting for evaluation of breast reduction. The patient has attempted nonsurgical treatments, but the minimal relief.
• Medical Reasoning: The patient is an ideal candidate for bilateral reduction mammoplasty based on her measurements (BSA 2.65) and symptoms (symptomatic macromastia).
• Medical Reasoning: Her minimum required resection based on BSA of 2.65 using the Schnur scale is 1792 grams which should be attainable given her extremely large breasts and measurements above.
• Medical Reasoning: There is potential for using a nipple graft given the size of the breasts.
• Medical Treatment Plan: We discussed options today including surgical options such as bilateral reduction mammoplasty as well as nonsurgical options such as weight loss or wearing a sports bra more often to alleviate symptoms. We discussed risks and benefits of each option today as well as what to expect postoperatively including activity restrictions after surgery such as no heavy lifting or driving for two to three weeks after surgery until drains are removed in clinic after one week postoperatively.
• Patient Education: I explained all of these options today including risks and benefits of each option today as well as what to expect postoperatively including activity restrictions after surgery such as no heavy lifting or driving for two to three weeks after surgery until drains are removed in clinic after one week postoperatively.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Renal ultrasound due to hematuria.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Kelly Wood is a 41-year-old female who presents today for a renal ultrasound due to hematuria. She reports that she passed two stones last week and has had several episodes of bright red urine the color of cherry kool-aid over the past 6 weeks. She also reports constant urination and severe pain last week. She rates her pain as an 8 on a scale of 0 to 10, with 0 being no pain and 10 being the worst possible pain. She denies flank pain or tenderness in her lower back.

Ms. Wood reports that she drinks more Mountain Dew than water daily.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Urinary: Hematuria.
• Constitutional: Pain.
• Neurological: No back pain.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

• Constitutional: Tolerates examination well. Reports constant urination and severe pain last week. Denies flank pain or tenderness in her lower back.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Urine dipstick today. Negative for leukocytes, nitrates, protein, ketone, bilirubin and glucose. Color yellow and clear, urobilinogen 0.2 EU/dL, pH 5.5 and specific gravity 1.020. There is a trace amount of blood in the urine and intact.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Ms. Wood is a 41-year-old female who presents today for a renal ultrasound due to hematuria.
Primary diagnosis: Hematuria.
Secondary diagnosis: Chronic urolithiasis.
Medical Reasoning: The patient's renal ultrasound today revealed a left kidney stone non-obstructing but she did pass two stones last week so we discussed dietary modifications to prevent future stones with her today.
Medical Treatment: I advised the patient that she should drink about half of her body weight in ounces of water a day (125 ounces) and avoid sugary drinks like Mountain Dew as well as foods rich in sodium oxalate such as spinach, chocolate, beets, rhubarb and soy products because they are high in sodium which can increase stone formation.
Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with recommended medical treatment.

Cardiovascular: Reports chest pain.
Respiratory: Reports shallow breathing.

note.objective_results:
RESULTS

note.assessment_and_plan:

Status post mitral valve repair.

• Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan.

note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Cardiovascular: Normal S1 and S2 is preserved with a normal rate and regular rhythm. There is a 4/6 systolic murmur at the right upper sternal border with mild radiation to the carotids.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Diana Scott is a 100-year-old female who presents today for evaluation of a new worrisome heart murmur.

Probable one cardiac murmur.
- Medical Reasoning: Her 4/6 systolic murmur at the right upper sternal border with mild radiation to the carotids is most likely representative of aortic stenosis, given her symptoms could be due to severe aortic stenosis. However, her S2 is relatively preserved, which would be more consistent with moderate. Some of her outside records do note diastolic dysfunction, so it is possible she did have an echocardiogram at some point in the past. She does not appear significantly volume overloaded today.
- Medical Treatment: We will order an echocardiogram to assess overall cardiac structure and function as well as valve view of where disease may be present. Depending on results as well as the severity of her aortic stenosis, we will need to consider an ischemic evaluation or further possibly a heart monitor to assess overall burden of the PVCs. At this point she is asymptomatic so we will start with the echocardiogram only.
- Patient Education and Counseling: I discussed all findings and recommendations with the patient today and she understands.

The patient denies any nasal congestion, rhinorrhea, or throat swelling. He does report eye water, which he attributes to allergies.

The patient denies any rash, nausea, or vomiting.

The patient reports that his symptoms are worse when near his cat or outside the house. They have been present in all three situations.

He denies any travel-related symptoms at this time.

• Cardiovascular: No chest pain or dyspnea at rest.
• Gastrointestinal: Diarrhea after consuming large amounts of alcohol.

note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Charles Sullivan is a pleasant 45-year-old male who presents today for evaluation of new onset dyspnea. The patient reports that he has noticed that his breathing is not what it used to be. He states that he seems to catch his breath a lot more than he used to and considers himself to be pretty healthy. He denies any previous issues with allergies.
• New onset allergic asthma.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient’s history and examination findings are consistent with newly diagnosed allergic asthma as evidenced by the presence of expiratory wheezing bilaterally in all lung fields on auscultation and the lack of other findings consistent with other diagnoses such as heart failure or COPD.
- Medical Treatment: I have prescribed albuterol inhaler for him to use as needed for symptoms and have prescribed Singulair 10 mg once daily for him to take daily in hopes of decreasing the frequency of his asthma attacks. We will proceed with allergy testing today and if we are unable to identify triggers from skin testing we will discuss additional testing in blood and immunotherapy options at our next visit.
- Patient Education: I have explained the nature of allergic asthma and recommended lifestyle modifications such as avoiding known allergens including cats, dogs, dust mites, etc., as well as avoiding alcohol consumption which may exacerbate symptoms due to dehydration.
- Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan.

Bryan Brooks is a 39-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of back pain. The onset of his symptoms began yesterday when he was raking leaves. He has tried icing and Advil, but this did not help. The patient reports that the only thing that helped was a hot shower and it feels better when he sits. He states that he normally does not do any physical activity.

The patient reports that his partner also has been experiencing back pain today, but reports that it is worse when standing up. The patient believes this is due to his partner's higher pain tolerance.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Gregory Hernandez is a pleasant 40-year-old male who presents today for evaluation of a non-healing right foot ulcer.
• Non-healing diabetic foot ulcer.
- Medical Reasoning: This appears to be related to his poorly controlled diabetes as evidenced by his elevated A1C level and recent onset of symptoms including redness and drainage from this wound.
- Patient Education and Counseling: I discussed with him today that this could be related to his poorly controlled diabetes and advised him to follow up with his primary care physician for further treatment recommendations as well as review how to properly monitor his blood sugar levels at home.
- Medical Treatment Plan:
- Order ABI ankle brachial index just to determine blood supply in his foot to see if we can actually heal this ulcer.
- Perform debridement here just to take off some dead tissue.
- Prescribe clindamycin 400 mg twice daily for 7 days to try to get rid of infection which you currently do have and that will get rid of some redness and drainage which is happening now.
- Obtain surgical shoe for next month while this is happening.

note.assessment_and_plan:

Left ankle sprain.

The blister soon became a wound and he was seen by his PCP. He was placed on a round of antibiotics, which he completed yesterday. Neurological: Reports neuropathy.

note.objective_exam:

note.objective_results:

note.assessment_and_plan:

Diabetic Foot Ulcer.

We will continue this until we see improvement in wound size and pink tissue present. He will wear surgical shoe to take pressure off area until we see improvement in wound size and pink tissue present.
- Patient Education/ Counseling: We discussed options for treatment today including debridement in office as well as prescription collagenase ointment for home use.
- Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with recommended medical treatment plan.

Right knee pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

William Russell is a pleasant 57-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for evaluation of right knee pain. The patient reports that he injured his right knee while at the trampoline park with his wife. He heard a snap and instant pain when he landed on the trampoline. He denies any history of similar injuries. The patient states that he does not work out regularly and has tried to maintain a regular exercise regimen but has been inconsistent with it. He denies taking any medications for pain control, but reports using Tylenol occasionally. The patient states that he has elevated blood pressure and is currently taking lisinopril 20 mg daily, however, he does not consistently take his medication. He denies measuring his blood pressure recently and notes that he is not suspicious of this.

The patient also reports that he has type 2 diabetes and is currently taking metformin 500 mg daily. He states that he checks his blood sugars most days when he remembers to do so, but notes that this is inconsistent. He states that he checks his blood sugars 4-5 times per week and would like to switch to checking them twice daily. The patient notes that his diet has been decent but admits to not being consistent with it.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Right knee pain.
Cardiovascular: Elevated blood pressure.
Endocrinology: Type 2 diabetes mellitus.
note.objective_exam:

Neurological: Normal sensation in all extremities.
Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm without murmurs auscultated bilaterally.
Respiratory: Lungs are clear bilaterally.

note.objective_results:

note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Right knee pain.
- Medical Reasoning: This appears to be a lateral ligament strain based on examination findings today.
- Medical Treatment Plan: I have prescribed meloxicam 15 mg daily for pain and swelling. I have referred him to physical therapy today as well to help strengthen the muscles around the area and prevent further injury if needed. If symptoms persist we can consider further imaging in the future as this is a common injury that tends to heal on its own.
- Patient Education/ Counseling Plan: I have educated him on proper home care including icing, elevation, etc., as well as recommended physical therapy today for strengthening exercises.
- Patient Agreements/Consent Obtained: Patient understands and agrees with recommended medical treatment plan.

Back pain.

Matthew Hill is a pleasant 44-year-old male who presents today for evaluation of back pain. The patient reports that his back pain has been worsening over the past month. He states that he has been unable to play football due to his back pain. The patient reports that he has been bedridden due to his back pain and cannot tie his shoes or stand for long periods of time. He notes that sitting and laying down make his symptoms better. Neurological: Denies numbness or tingling in lower extremities or weakness in legs.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

MSK: Examination of the lumbar spine reveals tenderness to palpation at L4 vertebrae bilaterally.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

MRI of the lumbar spine reveals a disk herniation at L4-5 vertebrae with nerve root impingement.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Matthew Hill is a pleasant 44-year-old male who presents today for evaluation of back pain.

The patient presents today with acute disk herniation at L4-L5 with associated nerve root impingement causing lower back and left leg pain.
Medical Reasoning: The MRI revealed a disk herniation at L4-L5 with associated nerve root impingement, which explains the patient's symptoms.
Medical Treatment: I recommended an epidural steroid injection today, as well as continued physical therapy and strengthening exercises. We will follow up in 1 month.
Patient Education and Counseling: I advised him that this can take about 2-3 weeks for the epidural steroid injection to take full effect, and we will continue physical therapy until then.
INSTRUCTIONS
The patient will follow up with me in 1 month.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Headaches.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Julie Jenkins is a 33-year-old female who presents today for evaluation of headaches. She was referred to me by her primary care provider. She reports that she has been struggling with headaches for years now ever since she was a teenager and they used to be around her when she would have her menstrual menses but as she got older she noticed that it has been with that and also she can get it when she is really stressed. Recently, however, and why she went to her primary care provider is because her headaches have been getting a lot more frequent and severe. She states that they are mostly on the right side and it even seems like it’s behind her eye and it just like this pulsing like this really bad pulsing sensation. She notes that they seem to get worse around her menstrual periods but also when she is exercising. She denies any numbness or tingling to her hands or feet or face. She does experience ringing in the ears for a few months now and then what really scared her is that now she’s starting to get some blurred vision on the side of her vision.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Headache: Yes.
• Vestibular: Yes.
• Vision: Yes.
• Neurological: Yes.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Neurological Examination:
- Cranial nerves 1-12 are intact including normal cranial reflexes.
- Gait is normal.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

The patient today presents for evaluation of headaches. Her symptoms are concerning for idiopathic intracranial hypertension, which is increased pressure in the brain without any known cause for it. This can lead to permanent changes in vision if left untreated. We discussed this with the patient today, and I advised that we need to obtain an MRI of the brain today in order to confirm this diagnosis. We will also be performing a lumbar puncture today as well as referring the patient to a neuro-ophthalmologist for a complete eye exam.

Patient Agreements Obtained: The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Neck pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Jack Torres is a pleasant 40-year-old male who presents today for evaluation of neck pain. The onset of his neck pain began approximately 1 week ago after he was in a motor vehicle accident where he hit the back of his head and neck. He reports that the pain is localized to the back of his neck and worsens with movement. He rates his pain as an 8 out of 10, but it is not constant. He has tried ibuprofen, which has helped somewhat, but not completely. The patient denies any headaches or hearing or visual disturbances. He does report that he had some headaches early on but they have resolved. The patient denies any swelling or bruising to his neck.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Neck: Reports neck pain.
• Head: Reports headaches.
• Neurological: Denies numbness, tingling, weakness, or balance issues.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Neck: Positive pain to palpation of the soft tissues of the neck. Positive pain with flexion and extension.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-ray of cervical spine obtained today shows no signs of fracture or bony abnormalities.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

The patient presents today for evaluation of neck strain secondary to a motor vehicle accident 1 week ago. I reviewed the results of his x-ray today which showed no signs of fracture or bony abnormalities.

TREATMENT PLAN
I have recommended conservative treatment for this patient including anti-inflammatory medication Motrin 600 mg every 6-8 hours as needed and Flexeril 10 mg every 12 hours as needed. I advised him to try to relax his neck and avoid straining it further at this time. We will also order an MRI to rule out any nerve impingement or concussion due to whiplash symptoms.
I have recommended that we refer him to either physical therapy or chiropractic care once we receive the results from the MRI.

Bobby Flores is a pleasant 56-year-old male who presents today for evaluation of right shoulder pain.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Right elbow pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

William Smith is a 45-year-old male who presents today with right elbow pain. The patient reports that he has been playing a lot of tennis recently, as his friend has been encouraging him to get off the couch and be more active. He has been hitting the court a lot more and it has been killing him for the last three weeks or so. The patient states that he is experiencing pain in the outside part of his right elbow. He denies any radiation of pain to his arm or shoulder. The patient rates his pain as an 8 out of 10 when using his right arm, but it is only a 3 when resting. The patient describes the pain as sharp, shooting, and throbbing.

The patient denies any trauma recently, falling on his right elbow or feeling a pop anywhere. He notes that he has taken Tylenol and ibuprofen but they do not help with the pain once they wear off.

The patient reports that he has tried icing his right elbow but it does not help much.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Right elbow pain.
Neurological: No numbness or tingling in extremities.
Cardiovascular: Grade 3 systolic ejection murmur.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Cardiovascular: Grade 3 out of 6 systolic ejection murmur heard at the left lower sternal border which is unchanged from prior exam. Otherwise unremarkable examination.
Musculoskeletal: Examination of the right elbow reveals moderate lateral epicondylar tenderness. Pain with passive range of motion of the right elbow. No palpable joint effusion. Mild pain with resisted extension of the right wrist.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-ray findings reveal no acute fracture or other bony abnormality. There is no malalignment or sign of joint effusion.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

William Smith is a 45-year-old male who presents today with right elbow pain.
Acute lateral epicondylitis of the right elbow (tennis elbow).
Medical Reasoning: This is likely due to overuse likely from increased tennis activity which normally would be good but maybe we are overdoing it a little bit.
Medical Treatment Plan: I have recommended that he rest his right arm as much as possible for the next four to six weeks and avoid repetitive stress in that arm as well. I have recommended icing his right elbow for twenty minutes at least three times per day which should reduce pain and inflammation. I have also prescribed him Ultram 50 mg once per day to help with his discomfort from this injury. I will also prescribe him a brace for his forearm to help with discomfort from this injury today before he leaves my office. We will follow up in four weeks at that time we will reevaluate his elbow at that time and if needed we will consider additional imaging such as an MRI possibly along with a physical therapy referral depending on how he is doing.
Medical Treatment Plan for Diabetes Type Two:
The patient’s blood sugars were slightly elevated today compared to prior visits where they were running low in the low one hundreds and two hundreds range where they are now running around one fifty-one sixty due to Easter and eating too many Cadbury eggs which are deadly! We need to make some adjustments today so I have increased his metformin dosage from 500 mg twice daily to 1000 mg twice daily today which should help bring down those blood sugars slightly better than before. We will check these results again in two weeks after we review them together again at our next visit along with an HgbA1c level and CBC blood test today as well as a chem-12 blood test tomorrow morning after reviewing these results together again we can make additional adjustments if needed at that time.
Medical Treatment Plan for Mild Intermittent Asthma:
The patient’s asthma remains under good control today so we will continue him on Flovent twice daily and albuterol as needed without any changes there today. He can use these medications as tolerated but does need a refill on albuterol so I have written him a prescription for this refill which can be picked up at your pharmacy tomorrow morning after reviewing these results together again.

I will also prescribe him a brace for his forearm to help with discomfort from this injury today before he leaves my office. note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Asthma.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Betty Lewis is a pleasant 66-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for worsening asthma symptoms. The patient reports that she has been frustrated with her asthma as she has been unable to catch a break and has always been coughing and wheezing. She notes that her asthma flares up when she gets sick with a cold, but she also had a flare-up after going to her aunt's house. She denies any history of seasonal allergies, smoking, or vaping. She occasionally goes to bars that allow smoking inside, which bothers her.

The patient reports that she usually ends up going to urgent care or her primary care provider for these symptoms. She has had several visits in the past year where they have started her on prednisone taper packs and sometimes high doses over 5 days. She also mentions that she has had several visits in the past year where they have prescribed antibiotics and steroids.

The patient reports that she last needed to be hospitalized due to her asthma symptoms about a month ago.

The patient denies any history of smoking or vaping. She does enjoy hiking but does not have any trouble getting out and doing so due to seasonal allergies. She does not enjoy going over to her aunt's house because of the cat there.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Respiratory: Dyspnea on exertion.
Cardiovascular: Palpitations.
Neurological: Headache.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm without murmurs, gallops, or rubs.
Respiratory: Diminished lung sounds throughout with occasional expiratory wheeze bilaterally.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Pulmonary function test obtained today is consistent with asthma.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Betty Lewis is a pleasant 66-year-old female who presents today for worsening asthma symptoms consistent with moderate intermittent asthma. I reviewed the results of her pulmonary function test today which were consistent with asthma. We discussed treatment options today including initiating Flovent one hundred ten micrograms one puff twice per day as this will help prevent daily symptoms and reduce the need for rescue inhaler use. We also discussed an action plan for managing exacerbations of symptoms as well as how we can work on avoiding triggers such as cats at this time.
INSTRUCTIONS
Continue taking Flovent one hundred ten micrograms one puff twice per day as prescribed. Continue using Ventolin inhaler two puffs every 4-6 hours prn.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Back pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Larry Garcia is a pleasant 41-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for evaluation of back pain. The patient reports that he has been experiencing back pain for the past 2 years. He states that he started having back pain after moving furniture one weekend. The patient describes his pain as sharp and stabbing in nature, radiating down to his right leg, and even down to his toe. He also reports that he is unable to get comfortable, which is worse when he sits down. The patient denies any numbness or tingling in the genital or rectal area. He does report some numbness and tingling in his right leg that goes down to his foot. The patient denies any loss of sensation in the genital or rectal area. He also denies any weakness.

The patient reports that he has had difficulty with bladder or bowel control.

The patient has tried physical therapy before, but this was only temporary and they have even prescribed him strong pain medications. He was also recommended surgery in the past but would like to avoid surgery.

The patient used to play golf but has been unable to due to his back pain.

PAST HISTORY

Patient reports a history of chronic lumbar back pain.
SOCIAL HISTORY

Patient quit smoking 20 years ago.
FAMILY HISTORY

Patient denies any family history of spine conditions.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Musculoskeletal: Examination of the lumbar spine reveals no erythema or ecchymosis overlying the midline tenderness at L4-L5 disk space with right-sided lumbar paravertebral tenderness.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS
MRI of the lumbar spine reveals disc herniation with nerve impingement.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Chronic lumbar back pain.
Based on your symptoms, exam, and reviewing your MRI results, your symptoms are consistent with an L4-L5 herniated disk with radiculopathy.
I recommend a spinal injection with a strong inflammatory medication called a corticosteroid today. We will inject the corticosteroid into your lumbar spine under fluoroscopy which you can think of as an x-ray to help localize to the exact area of your pain. This should help reduce inflammation that is causing your pain. We will monitor you and see how you respond to this injection and we will schedule you for another injection if needed at intervals of 4 times per year. This procedure is relatively quick and common and you should be out of the office within an hour.

Right knee pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Kenneth King is a pleasant 44-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for right knee pain. The patient reports that he was getting ready for the holiday weekend and was out on his boat skiing. He did a jump and twisted when he landed and his knee has been hurting him ever since. He denies hearing anything pop or feeling anything pop at the time of injury. He was able to get out of the water by himself but it was very sore to climb up and any kind of squatting or bending is really pretty sore. The patient denies ever having injured this knee before. He is a frequent water skier.

The patient reports that he has been taking lisinopril 20 mg once a day for hypertension. His blood pressure at home has been about 125/80 most of the days. He denies any side effects from lisinopril.

The patient reports that he has been taking Aleve twice a day for pain relief, as well as applying a cold pack to his right knee.

The patient denies any numbness or tingling in his foot.

Musculoskeletal: Right knee pain.
Neurological: No numbness or tingling in the right foot.

Right knee pain.

We can just go ahead and refer him to physical therapy to strengthen those muscles around his knee so that he does not have another injury in the future. I have prescribed meloxicam 15 mg once daily which will help take down swelling and help with some of the pain as well as prevent upset stomachs or anything like that.

Incidentally found right upper lobe lung nodule.

• Patient Education:
The patient understands and agrees with this plan.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Difficulty swallowing.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Tyler Green is a 56-year-old male who presents today complaining of difficulty swallowing. He has a past medical history of diabetes and hypertension. He is currently taking metformin 500 mg twice a day and Norvasc. The patient reports that he has noticed difficulty swallowing for the last 4-5 weeks. He states that it seems like something is always stuck in his throat, and he goes about his day with this issue. He describes it as being painful at times, but he does not have to worry about choking. When he swallows solid foods, he feels like he needs a little help pushing them down. The patient denies coughing with this issue, but does admit to thinking about potentially choking on occasion. He denies any blood in his stools or vomiting.

The patient reports that his diabetes is doing well since we last saw him. He states that he takes his medications as prescribed and feels good overall otherwise. The patient reports that he checks his blood sugars once in a while when he is in a hurry, but usually checks them 80% of the time.

The patient denies any nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea from metformin.

The patient denies chest pain or shortness of breath with this issue.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Cardiovascular: Denies chest pain or shortness of breath.
• Respiratory: Denies hemoptysis.
• Gastrointestinal: Denies hematochezia or vomiting.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Neck: No swelling in the neck; normal thyroid; no masses; no lymph nodes.
Respiratory: Lungs are clear bilaterally.
Cardiovascular: No murmurs heard on auscultation of the heart.
Gastrointestinal: Epigastric tenderness right here in the right upper quadrant.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Tyler Green is a 56-year-old male who presents today for evaluation of difficulty swallowing.

Difficult swallowing is concerning for esophageal stricture which can be from scar tissue formation secondary to reflux disease. I have referred him to gastroenterology for endoscopy and dilation if needed.
I recommended we start him on Prilosec 20 mg once daily to help with possible reflux exacerbating this issue.
I recommended we repeat his hemoglobin A1c today as I believe diet modification has been effective thus far and we should see improvement with these results.
I recommended we order some additional labs today including kidney function testing due to recent weight loss and hypertension control issues.
I recommended we obtain an eye referral for diabetic retinopathy screening due to recent weight loss and hypertension control issues.
Continue metformin at 500 mg twice daily as tolerated by the patient today.
Continue Norvasc as prescribed today.
The patient will follow up with me in one month for review of labs and additional symptoms if needed.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Right ankle pain and instability.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Jerry Cook is a 45-year-old male who presents today with right ankle pain and instability. The patient reports that his son Sean, who is 10 years old, was playing basketball at the courts and was more aggressive than the other players. The patient went up for a shot and Sean found him while he was going for a lap. The patient then landed awkwardly and rolled and twisted his right ankle. He notes that he has been experiencing bruising, swelling, and difficulty walking. The patient recently got back into working out and had been in a good rhythm going to the gym. He does not want to disrupt this routine.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports right ankle pain and instability.
Skin: Reports right ankle bruising and swelling.
Works from home and plans to coach his son’s basketball team in 04/2022.
Enjoys working out and recently resumed engaging in a consistent gym routine.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

MSK: Examination of the right ankle reveals swelling on the lateral side of the ankle. There is exquisite tenderness laterally over the lateral malleolus as well as tenderness over the medial deltoid region.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-rays were obtained today, not yet reviewed.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Lateral malleolar fracture of the right ankle.
Medical Reasoning: This is a Weber C type fracture due to displacement of the lateral malleolus. This is unstable due to its location.
Medical Treatment: I have discussed this with the patient today. We have discussed that he will need surgery to stabilize this fracture. We will proceed with an open reduction internal fixation (ORIF) with plate and screws. He will be non-weight-bearing for approximately 3 months while healing occurs. We discussed that he may need to sit out coaching until then but we can work on getting him back into coaching once he has healed sufficiently.
Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with this plan.

Anthony Miller is a 54-year-old male who presents today for evaluation of facial pain. The patient reports that he has had stabbing, shooting pain in his right cheekbone area for approximately 2-3 months. The pain is sometimes described as “hot” and he has noticed episodes where the pain is excruciating and lasts for a few minutes to an hour. The patient denies any sensory loss or weakness on the right side of his face. He denies left-sided facial pain, numbness, or tingling. He denies any history of multiple sclerosis or brain tumors. The patient endorses occasional headaches but no history of migraines.

The patient reports that certain temperatures and cold weather seem to trigger his symptoms. He has tried ibuprofen and motrin but these have not helped. He has also tried applying Tiger Balm to the area but this did not help either.

The patient notes that he has been seen by his family doctor who recommended that he come to see me today.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Neurological: Denies vision changes or weakness in right eye.
• Headache: Reports headaches.
• Sensory: Denies left-sided facial pain, numbness, or tingling in the right cheek.

Neurological: Examination of cranial nerves is intact bilaterally. No facial weakness noted on examination.

RESULTS

Neck pain.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Follow-up of chronic problems.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Carolyn Garcia is a 49-year-old female who presents today for follow-up of her chronic problems. She reports that her osteoarthritis has been flaring up a little bit lately, primarily in her elbows. She has been sitting at the computer, at the desk more in the office and does not know if it is being stagnant in that position all day which has increased flare-ups for that. She would like to discuss this further today.

She reports that she is right-handed and that her right elbow bothers her more than the other. She denies any other joint pain. She does report numbness and tingling in her hands when she is typing for long periods of time, but tries to shake out her arms to relieve this sensation.

She also reports that she had an episode of gout three months ago with inflammation of her toe. She states that the medication prescribed by me really controlled it and she has not seen a flare-up since.

Regarding psoriasis, she states that it has been under control and has not been a major problem for her either.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports right elbow pain.
Neurological: Reports numbness and tingling in hands.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

CV: Regular rate and rhythm.
Respiratory: Lungs are clear bilaterally.
MSK: Examination of cervical lymphadenopathy was unremarkable. Examination of the right elbow reveals edema, inflammation of the right olecranon, tenderness, effusion, pain with palpation of the olecranon bursa, pain with pronation and supination, pain with flexion and extension.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Autoimmune panel was reviewed today. The results were unremarkable. ESR was elevated. Uric acid was elevated.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Follow-up of chronic problems.
- Gout: Stable.
- Osteoarthritis: Right elbow edema, inflammation of the olecranon bursa, tenderness, effusion, pain with palpation of the olecranon bursa, pain with pronation and supination, pain with flexion and extension.
- Psoriasis: Stable.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's elevated ESR suggests possible systemic inflammatory process or rheumatoid arthritis; however, given her age and history of osteoarthritis alone this is unlikely. Her elevated uric acid level suggests gout which is stable currently as evidenced by no recent flare-ups despite discontinuation of colchicine 0.6 mg twice daily as needed for gout flare-ups.
- Medical Treatment Plan: Continue colchicine 0.6 mg twice daily as needed for flare-ups of gout. Order a right elbow x-ray today to evaluate for possible osteoarthritis. Prescribe meloxicam 15 mg once daily for pain and swelling due to osteoarthritis until x-rays are reviewed next week. Continue clobetasol cream for scalp psoriasis as tolerated.

Peptic Ulcer Disease:

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Swimming-related right knee pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Rebecca Thompson is a 27-year-old female who presents today for evaluation of right knee pain. The onset of her symptoms began last week and over the course of the month she has been swimming more regularly. She has been trying to get up and get active. She reports that all of a sudden she has been experiencing right knee pain while swimming. She denies any history of trauma to the right knee. She notes that she was able to swim 10 laps before the pain started, but after a couple laps it starts to hurt. She denies any swelling in her joints, but does have pain with range of motion of the knee and pain with patellar inhibition.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Reports no fevers or chills.
• Musculoskeletal: Reports right knee pain while swimming.
• Neurological: Denies numbness or tingling in her legs.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

• Neurological: Examination of the extremities is essentially normal. There is no weakness, atrophy, or sensory loss in the lower extremities.
• Musculoskeletal: Examination of the bilateral knees reveals no swelling. There is tenderness over the patella bilaterally with patellar inhibition.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-ray of the right knee was obtained today and reviewed by me in clinic today. The x-ray was normal.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Rebecca Thompson is a 27-year-old female who presents today for evaluation of right knee pain.
• Chondromalacia of the patella.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient presents today for evaluation of right knee pain which began last week and over the course of the month she has been swimming more regularly. She denies any history of trauma to her right knee, but reports that she was able to swim 10 laps before the pain started, but after a couple laps it starts to hurt. Examination reveals tenderness over her patella bilaterally with patellar inhibition.
- Medical Treatment: I recommended that we start anti-inflammatory medications such as ibuprofen 600 mg four times daily with food to help reduce inflammation in her knees. I also recommended that she do straight leg raising exercises to strengthen her quadriceps and help with her pain.
- Patient Education: I advised her that she should avoid anything that puts extra pressure on her knees for a little while and if it's not getting better in a couple weeks we will follow up again.
• Chronic back pain.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient reports that this has been doing well until recently when it flared up again last week after swimming more than usual.
- Medical Treatment: We discussed continuing with swimming as tolerated as this will help strengthen her back muscles which should help alleviate some symptoms from chronic back pain.
- Patient Education: We discussed continuing with current treatment plan including physical therapy and continued use of anti-inflammatory medications such as ibuprofen 600 mg four times daily with food as needed for flare-ups.
• Depression.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient reports that this has been stable since starting therapy and medication approximately 3 months ago, however she continues to experience some depressive symptoms which are impacting her quality of life at times.
- Medical Treatment: We discussed continuing with current treatment plan including continued use of antidepressants such as sertraline as prescribed by primary care provider until further notice.
- Patient Education: We discussed continued use of antidepressants such as sertraline as prescribed by primary care provider until further notice due to continued depressive symptoms impacting quality of life at times.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Yearly asthma, allergic rhinitis, and food allergy follow-up.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Emily Hernandez is a 20-year-old female who presents today for a yearly follow-up for asthma, allergic rhinitis, and food allergies. She was switched from Symbicort to Wixela due to insurance changes since her last office visit in April 2020. She also uses Zyrtec in the spring, summer, and fall for her seasonal allergy symptoms which tend to work well. She also has known peanut allergy and tolerates almonds and cashews. Her Asthma Control Test (ACT) score is 21.

The patient reports that she has been doing well overall. She notes that she has not had any urgent care or ER visits for breathing over the past year. She denies prednisone use for breathing issues.

She notes that she has been trying to reduce smoking and vaping in preparation for joining the military. She is currently trying to reduce smoking but still vapes occasionally. She hopes to be enlisted early spring of 2022.

The patient reports that she completed a breathing test today.

Allergies: The patient reports that she uses Zyrtec more during the spring and fall than summer. She does take it on days she knows she will be outside a lot, especially when working outside about 3 days per week. The patient denies having any reactions since her experience with peanuts at Enterprise Rent-a-Car last year.

The patient reports that she has been avoiding peanuts but recalls eating some almonds at one point after discussing with me if she might not be allergic anymore.

SOCIAL HISTORY

The patient reports that she currently smokes tobacco and vapes, trying to reduce and interested in cessation in preparation for joining the military.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Respiratory: Reports no respiratory symptoms including shortness of breath or wheezing.
Cardiovascular: Reports no chest pain or palpitations.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Ears: Normal appearance bilaterally with minimal cerumen noted bilaterally.
Nose: No nasal polyps or congestion noted.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Yearly asthma, allergic rhinitis, and food allergy follow-up.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's most recent Asthma Control Test (ACT) score was 21 which is considered excellent control of asthma symptoms. Her most recent spirometry was about the same as it was two years ago but looks better today. This explains why her numbers were lower at that time due to smoke exposure last year. Her current treatment plan includes Wixela Inhub 250 mcg-50 mcg/dose powder for inhalation once in the morning and once at night as needed due to insurance changes since her last office visit in April 2020. The patient is currently using Zyrtec daily during spring, summer, and fall due to seasonal allergy symptoms which tend to work well for her. She tolerates almonds but avoids tree nuts due to peanut allergy.
- Medical Treatment Plan: We discussed options today regarding her current treatment plan including switching from Wixela Inhub 250 mcg-50 mcg/dose powder for inhalation once in the morning and once at night as needed due to insurance changes since her last office visit in April 2020 to alvesco 80 mcg twice daily as needed due to insurance coverage limitations with Kaiser Permanente Broadway pharmacy only once a day instead of twice daily would be acceptable because some people do need it only once a day. We discussed this option with regard to minimizing use of inhalers like wixela or alvesco only when ill or during smoke season unless they are getting too sick every month then we would pull back too much. We also discussed continuing with zyrtec as needed over-the-counter until we repeat spirometry in four months when we can document improvement from current treatment plan if needed by military standards.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Resistant hypertension.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Jordan Roberts is a 49-year-old male who presents today for evaluation of resistant hypertension. The patient reports that he was recently in the emergency room with high blood pressure and palpitations. He believes this was due to a panic attack, as he had consumed several cups of coffee and no breakfast on the day in question. The patient denies experiencing any additional episodes since that time.

The patient reports that he has had issues with his blood pressure since he was young. He notes that his family history is positive for hypertension. The patient has been recently started on Benicar HCT 40 mg/25 mg and Amlodipine 10 mg daily by his new primary care provider.

The patient reports that he checks his blood pressure at home every morning, and it has been running at about 146 to 155 lately. He notes that he is trying to reduce his salt intake, but admits to not doing so well with it.

The patient reports that he does try to walk on the treadmill when he can.

PAST HISTORY

Medical: Hypertension.
Family History: Several family members positive for hypertension.

CURRENT MEDICATIONS

Benicar HCT 40 mg/25 mg; Amlodipine 10 mg daily.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm. No murmurs, gallops, or rubs.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Resistant hypertension.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient is currently on three medications at maximum dose and his blood pressure remains elevated. His potassium level was last checked one week ago and was found to be 4.0, which is within normal limits. However, we discussed the possibility of secondary causes of hypertension including hyperaldosteronism which can be treated with spironolactone. We discussed the possible side effects of spironolactone including electrolyte disturbances and gynecomastia as well as dehydration from decreased fluid intake which can cause dizziness upon standing up.
- Medical Treatment: We have added spironolactone to his regimen today. We will need to monitor his potassium levels as well as perform a metabolic panel in two weeks to check sodium levels. If this does not control his blood pressure we will refer him to the resistant hypertension clinic for further evaluation.
- Patient Education: I have provided information regarding the dash diet plan which has been shown to lower blood pressure.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Return visit for IBS with functional abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Brittany Edwards is a pleasant 32-year-old female who was last seen in August of 2019 with flares of abdominal pain, who was diagnosed with irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) that was treated with Bentyl. She had a previous prescription for Reglan that she received from the emergency room that she used as needed for nausea. She was instructed to start a low dose fiber supplement, such as Citrucel, daily, probiotics to help with gas and bloating, Bentyl up to four times daily for intestinal cramping, and stop Reglan and use Zofran as needed. Neuromodulators such as Elavil and Buspar were discussed but not started.

Today she presents for a return visit due to worsening symptoms of IBS. The patient reports that she has been going out to eat some on Friday nights and Saturday nights and that she has had some spicy foods or shrimp. She notes that her gut probably does not always appreciate that. She has been experiencing increased bowel movements between 2-3 times per day. Her stools are formed. She notes that after eating at Friday's restaurant she tends to have more diarrhea. She is unsure if it is the food or alcohol or both. When not eating out or drinking alcohol, her symptoms are better but she still experiences cramping and sharp pains.

The patient denies any recent weight loss or unintentional weight gain.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Gastrointestinal: Positive for diarrhea, nausea, and abdominal pain.
• Neurological: Positive for sleep disturbances.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

• Respiratory: Lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally.
• Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Brittany Edwards is a pleasant female with irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) and functional abdominal pain aggravated by high stress, poor eating habits, and poor sleeping habits.

I have encouraged dietary and lifestyle modifications including starting a neuromodulator such as Elavil 25 mg at bedtime for IBS.
She can use Bentyl 20 mg as needed 30-45 minutes prior to eating out at a restaurant. She can also use Zofran if needed. However, I have encouraged her to reduce greasy and fatty foods and alcohol consumption.
We discussed the possibility of starting long-term medication such as Elavil which would take the place of Bentyl or Zofran when symptoms are present all the time instead of just isolated incidents.
She can continue taking Citrucel twice daily for regularity on days when she feels good.
I have advised her to drink plenty of water before drinking alcohol instead of sodas.
She will follow up in one month by emailing over mychart regarding any side effects or issues with elavil or if adjustments are needed.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Follow-up for adult hydrocephalus.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Christopher Watson is an 86-year-old male who returns in follow-up for adult hydrocephalus. This is his first visit since undergoing shunt surgery on August 1st, 2020.

The patient reports that prior to surgery, he was having progressive problems that affected his walking, thinking, and bladder control. He underwent shunt surgery on August 1st, 2020. A Medtronic Strata programmable shunt in the ventricular peritoneal configuration was programmed at a level of 2.0 and placed.

The patient reports that since the shunt surgery three months ago he has been doing much better. His gait has improved and he can now walk to the dining room without assistance. However, he still experiences times where his daughter has to help him with his gait. His bladder control did improve some after surgery but now seems to have leveled out as he is wearing diapers.

Regarding cognition, the patient states that he feels like he can have a normal conversation with him again.

The patient denies headaches or pain where the shunt is located as well as any pain in his abdomen.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
- Neurological: Constitutional significant for impaired ability to carry out daily functions. Negative for fever or unintentional weight loss.
- GU: Significant for urinary incontinence and wearing a diaper. Negative for genital sores, decreased or painful output.
- Neurological: Significant for continued walking impairment and cognitive impairment. Negative for headaches, recent falls or hallucinations.
- Psychiatric: Negative for depression excessive worrying or mood swings.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS
CT scan of the head from 10/15/2020 shows a frontal horn span at the level of Foramen of Munro of 4.6 cm with a third ventricular contour that is flat with a span of 10 mm; substantial small vessel ischemic change.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Mr Christopher Watson is an 86-year-old male who returns today in follow-up due to adult hydrocephalus.
Diagnosis:
• Adult hydrocephalus
Gait impairment,
Uinary incontinence and urgency,
Cognitive impairment.
The patient had undergone shunt placement on August 1st, 2020 which was confirmed today by CT scan which showed substantial small vessel ischemic change but no extra axial fluid collections were noted by radiologist who stated there were no other fluid collections noted on this scan either; however there was also evidence of blood fluid collection in right parietal region which I do not believe this caused any symptoms therefore we will leave it alone until next visit when we will reevaluate it then we can discuss changing it if needed at that time as well as continue monitoring this finding until then because I do not believe it needs intervention at this time given current symptoms are stable without any headaches or pain reported today either by him nor his daughter Theresa Watson.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Followup for hypertension.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Amanda Taylor is a 72-year-old female who presents today for follow-up of hypertension. She reports that she has been struggling with not drinking alcohol. She had previously discussed this with the provider last time, but they did not have time to discuss it in detail. She reports that she has been drinking 4-5 times per week for a while. She denies any recent travel or exposure to coronavirus. She has received her coronavirus vaccine on February 9th.

The patient reports that she is taking her blood pressure medications as prescribed, but only takes half of the lisinopril dose due to side effects of lethargy and headaches. She also takes the full dose of hydrochlorothiazide daily and denies chest tightness or pressure or shortness of breath.

The patient reports that she checks her blood pressure at home and notes that her numbers are lower in the morning than in the evening, where she runs anywhere from 130-145 over 95-100 on the bottom. However, when she sits for a while and then takes her blood pressure, it goes down. In the mornings, it is generally more normal where it is supposed to be.

She also notes that she takes her medicine in the morning when she gets up instead of in the evening.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Cardiovascular: Reports no chest tightness or pressure or shortness of breath.
Neurological: Reports no headache.
Psychiatric: Reports no anxiety or depression.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Constitutional: Alert and oriented x3. No signs of intoxication.
Neurological: Cranial nerves II-XII grossly intact. No focal neurologic deficits noted.
Cardiovascular: Unlabored breathing. Cardiac rhythm regular, no murmurs, gallops, or extra heart sounds noted.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Alcohol use disorder.
Medical Reasoning: The patient is drinking alcohol four to five days per week to excess. No tobacco use, no substance abuse, skin is moist, good trigger.
Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed naltrexone which we have previously discussed today. The injectable form will be started on May 17th and we reviewed side effects and risks today including nausea, headache, dizziness, anxiety, tiredness and trouble sleeping which should resolve within a few days. The potential benefit of alcohol cessation would be highly beneficial to her for many reasons including hypertension as well as other medical issues such as hypercholesterolemia and hyperlipidemia.
Medical Treatment Plan: We will continue with current medications including lisinopril 20 mg once daily; hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg once daily until we see how well she does with naltrexone injections starting on May 17th. We will schedule an additional follow-up visit in June around the time of her second naltrexone injection at which point we can review how well she did with naltrexone injections as well as discuss other medical issues such as hypercholesterolemia and hyperlipidemia at that time.
Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with recommended medical treatment plan.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Ongoing management of rheumatoid arthritis.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Thomas Nelson is a 72-year-old male who presents today for ongoing management of rheumatoid arthritis. The patient reports that his right knee was injected with a steroid injection on 03/04/2021. Since that time, he has been experiencing swelling in his right knee and leg. He rates his pain as a 3 out of 10, but typically rates it at 6. The swelling has been present for approximately two months. The patient notes that the swelling was only in the right knee prior to this time. He has been wearing compression socks frequently, but they have not helped with the swelling. He notes that he has slowed down due to the pain and swelling, but he is able to perform most activities until he sits for a long period of time and then gets up, which is difficult due to stiffness. The patient reports that he has been taking his medications regularly, including Xeljanz XR 11 mg daily and Celebrex 200 mg daily.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Right knee pain.
Cardiovascular: Reports hypertension.
Neurological: Reports stiffness in right leg.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Musculoskeletal: Examination of the right knee reveals mild effusion and warmth over the medial aspect of the knee. There is some pitting edema around the knee and ankle.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Fluid aspiration and steroid injection procedure.
The risks, benefits, and alternatives were explained. The risks of steroid injection were explained, including but not limited to: hypopigmentation, soft tissue atrophy, tendon ruptures, and transient hypoglycemia among others. Verbal consent was attained.
The right knee was accessed through the lateral approach with 3 milliliters of initially clear fluid then blood tinged fluid. Then the right knee was prepped in a standard fashion. The right knee was injected with 80 milligrams of triamcinolone and one milliliter of lidocaine.
The procedure was tolerated well with no complications.
Post-procedure instructions were given.
