note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Perioral dermatitis.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Jacqueline Miller is a 40-year-old female who presents today for follow-up of perioral dermatitis. The patient reports that she has been using doxycycline cream twice daily for the past two weeks, but she has noticed that her rash has plateaued and is not continuing to improve. She discontinued breastfeeding and started taking doxycycline at that time. She was prescribed MetroCream and sulfacetamide wash, but she discontinued use of MetroCream because she read about the risks associated with it. She has been using the sulfacetamide wash twice daily, but she notes that it is not drying her out too much. The patient denies using any other lotions or cleansers.

The patient reports that she started taking doxycycline once daily last week, and she noticed improvement in her rash. She would like to continue taking doxycycline twice daily until her rash resolves, then once daily for another week before stopping.

The patient also notes that she has been experiencing ocular rosacea symptoms including redness and tearing in her eyes. She discontinued use of clindamycin due to side effects.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Skin: Reports perioral dermatitis.
• Eyes: Reports ocular rosacea symptoms including redness and tearing in her eyes.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

• Skin: Fitzpatrick skin type IV, meaning you are not going to burn, you are going to sun tan. There are a few faint erythematous papules on bilateral medial cheeks.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Perioral dermatitis.
Rosacea, including ocular rosacea.
Medical Reasoning: The patient’s rash is not improving with doxycycline cream twice daily as prescribed. We discussed alternative treatment options today including Elidel cream which can be used off-label for perioral dermatitis. However, the cost of Elidel cream is prohibitive at this time. We discussed other topical options such as tacrolimus ointment which may be more affordable than Elidel cream.
Medical Treatment: Continue using the same face wash, continue with MetroCream after face wash application, increase use of doxycycline to twice daily until rash is resolved then once daily for another week before stopping. Continue Vanicream as needed for moisturizing dry skin.
Patient Education: I advised the patient on proper use of Vanicream and recommended Bruder Mask as needed for additional moisturization.
Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with recommended medical treatment plan.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Abdominal pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Michael Rodriguez is a pleasant 47-year-old male who presents today for evaluation of abdominal pain. The patient reports that he has been experiencing right upper quadrant pain for several weeks. He notes that the pain is located right underneath his ribs and describes it as a squeezing severe pain. The patient rates his pain an 8 on a scale of 0 to 10, with 10 being the worst pain he has ever experienced. The patient states that the pain comes and goes but when it does come, it is severe. He also reports that he gets nauseated and sick in his stomach when he experiences this pain.

The patient reports that the pain typically occurs immediately after eating but can also occur a couple of hours after eating. He denies fevers but does report low grade fevers at times. The patient denies vomiting.

The patient reports that he was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes approximately 3 months ago and has been managing it with diet and exercise. He notes that his diet was worse before he was diagnosed with diabetes but since then, he has cut back on sugar and started a keto diet which has resulted in weight loss of approximately 25 pounds.

The patient states that his symptoms have not improved with dietary modifications. He notes that fatty foods are a staple of his keto diet and have been difficult to cut out because they were so delicious.

The patient reports that both his mother and father had gallbladder disease and had to have their gallbladders removed.

The patient enjoys nature photography and states that he likes to get out into nature around spring time to take pictures near the river.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Respiratory: Lungs are clear bilaterally to auscultation.
Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm without murmurs, rubs or clicks.
Abdomen: Soft, non-distended abdomen; positive guarding to palpation in the right upper quadrant.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Abdominal ultrasound obtained at an outside facility shows multiple gallstones present in the gallbladder with some mild thickening. The common bile duct size is within normal limits at 4.1 mm.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Michael Rodriguez is a pleasant 47-year-old male who presents today for evaluation of abdominal pain.
I do believe you have some mild cholecystitis with gallstones I do not appreciate any frank obstruction but it looks like your gallbladder is inflamed and it looks like that's happened maybe over the last few weeks since you've been having those symptoms.
Since you have not had any improvement with dietary modifications I am going to make the recommendation that we do remove your gallbladder and I would like to perform a laparoscopic cholecystectomy.
The surgery will take about an hour to an hour and a half and you'll probably spend the night in the hospital because we just want to monitor you post procedure to make sure everything is okay you're still going to want avoid those high fat foods after surgery eat foods that are going to be high in fiber.
Do you have any questions about what our assessment and plan is for this?
The other thing I want briefly discuss is now your not your type two diabetes I want you to follow up with your physician just to make sure that you're handling your diabetes especially the fact that you're going to have surgery and those type of things we will just continue to monitor your diabetes as has been outlined by your endocrinologist or your primary care provider I'm going to have the nurse come in get some paperwork signed if you don't have any questions for me i will see you next week we will get this gallbladder out.

note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Scott Miller is a 36-year-old male who presents today for right knee pain.

Medical Reasoning:
Based on my examination today, Scott Miller's right knee injury is really suggestive of an anterior cruciate ligament tear. He has heard of this before, especially when people do sports and they injure their knees.
Medical Treatment:
I have recommended that we order an MRI today to evaluate the integrity of his ACL. We will follow up with him once we receive results from this exam.
In addition, I have prescribed meloxicam fifty milligrams daily for anti-inflammatory effects and pain relief.
The patient will also need to limit activities until we receive results from his MRI exam. I advised him to wear a knee immobilizer and use crutches when walking around until then.
The patient should also moderate his activities due to discomfort while sitting at work for long periods of time.
The patient should avoid jogging until we receive results from his MRI exam.
Patient Agreements:
The patient understands and agrees with recommended medical treatment plan.

Back pain.

note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Noah Scott is a pleasant 41-year-old male who presents today for evaluation of low back pain.

Medical Reasoning:
I believe this is a musculoskeletal low back strain based on his history and examination findings today. I ordered an x-ray today as well as a prescription for flexeril to help with his pain management today.
Regarding his diabetes, I believe it is well controlled based on recent blood sugar levels; however, we have not seen him in almost 5 months so I ordered an A1C today as well as recommended continued diet and exercise as well as continued metformin use at this time.
Regarding his eye issues, I recommended we follow up with ophthalmology today due to possible diabetic retinopathy secondary to poorly controlled diabetes.
I advised him that we will need to watch his intake of carbohydrates at the bakery due to possible weight gain from increased sugar intake from donuts and cakes. We discussed how often he should be checking his blood sugars in order for me to get an idea of how well he is managing them at home.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Dennis Martin is a pleasant 46-year-old male who presents today for evaluation of right heel pain.

Medical Reasoning:
This patient presents today with right heel pain that began 10 days ago. The patient describes his symptoms as located in the posterior aspect of his heel, radiating proximally into his calf. The patient states that his symptoms are aggravated by working out and when he first gets up in the morning. He runs 10 kilometers in the morning, bikes for 45 minutes to an hour at lunchtime, and swims for 30 minutes to an hour in the evening. He alternates between a long run and a long bike ride on weekends. He takes one day off from exercises and does not stretch at all.
I have reviewed this patient’s history today and believe this is likely due to Achilles tendinitis from overuse. This frequently occurs when someone starts training aggressively for an event.
I discussed this with him today and recommended we discontinue training for a week or two until we can monitor how he responds to treatment with ibuprofen or Advil every six hours as well as physical therapy visits to help strengthen his lower extremities and learn how to stretch those muscles before starting these activities again.
I advised him that I did not ask about medication today but I’m assuming whatever he was doing wasn’t working significantly so I’d like him to try ibuprofen or Advil every six hours.
I also recommended we order some physical therapy visits today so we can get some strength and stretching knowledge in before he starts these activities again.
We discussed options for further testing but I did not recommend x-rays at this time but if this continues without improvement after ten days then we may need more aggressive treatment plans such as cortisone injections or surgery.
Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with recommended medical treatment plan.

Christina Cooper is a 77-year-old female who presents today for evaluation of a non-healing right foot ulcer. The patient reports that the ulcer has been present for approximately 1 year. • Constitutional: Reports fatigue.
• Musculoskeletal: Reports decreased sensation in feet.

The patient denies any chest pain or shortness of breath with exertion.

The patient lives with his dog and is a San Francisco 49ers fan.

Aspirin; Brilinta; Fish oil; Crestor; Metoprolol 50 mg once a day.
note.objective_exam:

Neck: No jugular venous distention or carotid bruits.

note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Coronary artery disease.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient presents today for a follow-up visit after having a heart attack 6 months ago. He has been compliant with aspirin and Brilinta, but has been experiencing dizziness when standing up quickly. His most recent hemoglobin A1c was 16%, which is concerning for diabetes mellitus. The echocardiogram revealed a grade 3/6 systolic ejection murmur at the left base of the heart, which may be due to coronary artery disease.
- Medical Treatment: I have referred him for cardiac rehabilitation today to increase his activity level and confidence in exercising again. I have also refilled his metoprolol and Crestor 40 mg once daily as needed. We will continue to monitor him for symptoms of chest pain or shortness of breath with exertion.
- Patient Education: I discussed dietary modifications with him today as well as stress management techniques to help manage symptoms of depression.
- Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan.

She also reports that she has been drinking more alcohol than usual, but she does not think that this was the cause of her gastritis. The patient notes that her pain is located in both sides of her upper abdomen and increases when she works out, such as jogging or going for a run. She denies any nausea or vomiting with her abdominal pain, but she does report experiencing nausea 3 times in the past week and vomits a couple of times.

• Constitutional: Reports fever.
• Neurological: Denies headache.
• Psychiatric: Denies mood changes.

Gastrointestinal: Mild tenderness in epigastrium of abdomen otherwise soft abdomen no tenderness in right lower quadrant whatsoever no significant tenderness in right upper quadrant.
note.assessment_and_plan:

• Medical Reasoning: The patient presents today with new onset abdominal pain which is located in both sides of the upper abdomen and increases when she works out. Her history of diabetes type 2 and moderate alcohol use may have contributed to this new onset abdominal pain as well as increased coffee intake which may have triggered her gastritis.
• Medical Treatment: I have prescribed Zantac twice daily to help decrease acid production in the stomach and relieve symptoms of gastritis. We will also order a urinalysis, urine pregnancy test, CBC, comprehensive metabolic panel to rule out other causes for her symptoms. We will follow up in 4 weeks at this time.

Diabetes Type 2 Medical Reasoning: The patient’s blood sugars were elevated at last visit at 800 mg/dL so we will continue metformin at 1000 mg morning dose and 500 mg evening dose daily to help keep blood sugars under control.
Medical Treatment: Continue metformin as prescribed.

Medical Treatment: Continue Flovent daily and albuterol as needed for wheezing.
Patient Agreements: Patient understands and agrees with recommended medical treatment plan.

Alexis Gutierrez is a 33-year-old female who presents today for evaluation of right hand numbness and tingling. She reports that she has been experiencing these symptoms for approximately 6 months, but they have been more persistent over the last month. She states that she experiences some pain when typing on the keyboard, but the numbness and tingling are present all the time. She has been taking ibuprofen for pain relief, which seems to help when she stops typing on the keyboard. She also notes that her mouse causes her pain. The patient denies any nocturnal pain or sleep disruption.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports right hand numbness and tingling.
Neurological: Reports right hand pain.
note.objective_exam:

Neurological: Examination of the extremities reveals decreased grip strength in the right hand compared to her left. Tinel's sign is positive in the right wrist.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Alexis Gutierrez is a 33-year-old female who presents today for evaluation of right hand numbness and tingling.

Medical Reasoning: I believe this patient has carpal tunnel syndrome based on her history and examination findings today.
Medical Treatment Plan: I have recommended that we start with a wrist splint at night to help with her symptoms. We will also continue with ibuprofen, which she can take up to 600 mg four times daily. We will also order an EMG/nerve conduction study to further evaluate her symptoms. If this test comes back positive, we may consider physical therapy or surgery as needed at that time.

The patient reports that he has been doing well since being discharged from the hospital. He notes that he has been taking his medications as prescribed and has been watching his diet.

The patient denies chest pain, shortness of breath, or problems sleeping since being discharged from the hospital.

Cardiovascular: Reports shortness of breath.
Respiratory: Reports shortness of breath.
Neurological: Denies chest pain.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

VITALS: Blood pressure 128/72 mmHg; heart rate 79 bpm; respiratory rate 26; SpO2 99% on room air.
NECK: No jugular venous distension.
HEART: Grade 2/6 systolic ejection murmur which is stable.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

James Davis is an 82-year-old male with past medical history significant for hypertension and stage three chronic kidney disease who presents for hospital follow-up after an acute on chronic CHF exacerbation.

Congestive heart failure.
- Medical Reasoning: This appears to be caused by dietary indiscretion in an uncontrolled hypertension.
- Medical Treatment Plan: Continue bumex 2 mg once daily as prescribed. Continue watching diet and avoid salty foods. We will continue monitoring the systolic ejection murmur today which was heard before in clinic today. We will also order a renal artery ultrasound to rule out secondary causes of kidney disease today as well. Continue cozaar 100 mg daily and norvasc 5 mg once daily as prescribed today.
- Patient Education Plan: I have counseled the patient regarding dietary modifications today including limiting salt intake due to his love of pizza and chicken wings. I have also counseled him regarding weight monitoring today as well as ordering a renal artery ultrasound today due to his elevated blood pressure today.
- Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan.

Right ankle pain.

The patient enjoys playing soccer for the community league.

Ibuprofen as needed for pain.

note.objective_results:

Gregory Hernandez is a pleasant 42-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for evaluation of right ankle pain.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Elevated cholesterol.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Julie Cruz is a 17-year-old non-binary immensipated minor with no significant past medical history presents for evaluation of newly diagnosed hypercholesterolemia. She reports that she went for her annual checkup and they checked her cholesterol level, which was elevated. She was told to come in today.

The patient reports that she enjoys being outside and riding her bike on trails. She states that she keeps pretty active during the week. She also states that she likes to cook pretty much everything fresh, but she does enjoy chocolate chip cookies. She denies any issues with growing up or with bones feeling okay.

The patient denies any history of hypercholesterolemia or anemia at an early age. She does not recall any family members who had these issues. Her parents smoked when they lived with her, but she lives on her own now and nobody smokes in her apartment. The patient’s grandparents have told her that a cousin died at age 44 or 45 due to a heart attack.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Cardiovascular: Denies chest pain.
Musculoskeletal: Denies bone pain.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

VITALS: Blood pressure looks good.
NECK: No thyroid gland enlargement.
HEENT: No exophthalmos.
NEURO: No focal deficits.
CV: No murmurs, gallops, or rubs heard on auscultation of the heart.
RESPIRATORY: Lungs are clear bilaterally to auscultation.
GI: No hepatomegaly or splenomegaly palpable.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Cholesterol level was elevated at 210.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Elevated cholesterol.
• Medical Reasoning: The American Academy of Pediatrics recommends that all children be screened once they become between ages 9 and 11 and again between ages 17 and 20 years old. Studies have shown a link between high cholesterol and premature heart attacks. Therefore, I reviewed the results of the patient’s cholesterol level which was elevated at 210 mg/dL today, which is high for this age group. We discussed this today as well as other possible causes for the elevated cholesterol levels today including secondary causes such as diabetes mellitus, hypothyroidism, liver disease, etc., as well as familial causes such as genetic testing to see if this problem is familial or secondary cause.
• Medical Treatment Plan: We discussed dietary changes including a full cholesterol panel ordered today along with glucose testing, complete metabolic panel, thyroid studies, liver panels and genetic testing to see if this problem is familial or secondary cause. We also discussed lifestyle modifications including continued exercise such as biking which the patient enjoys doing regularly. We will follow up in 3-6 months after meeting with a nutritionist who can provide information about what kind of foods to eat.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Chest pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Elizabeth Scott is a 53-year-old female today complaining of chest pain. She has a past medical history of diabetes type 2 and high blood pressure. She is currently taking metformin 500 mg twice daily.

The patient reports that she has been experiencing chest pain for approximately three months. She states that the pain is mainly when she is walking, but it has been exacerbated by inactivity. The patient describes the pain as a dull pressure in her chest. She denies any radiation or exacerbating factors. She denies shortness of breath, sweating, or clamminess.

The patient reports that her blood sugars have been elevated due to inactivity and diet changes. She states that she has been trying to improve her diet and exercise but she has not been able to keep up with it due to the chest pain.

She denies any nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea with her diabetes.

PAST HISTORY

Medical: Diabetes type 2.
Family History: Heart disease.

CURRENT MEDICATIONS
Metformin 500 mg twice daily.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
- Cardiovascular: No jugular venous distention (JVD). No carotid bruits heard bilaterally.
- Respiratory: Lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally without wheezes, rales, rhonchi, or stridor.
- Cardiovascular: Grade 2/6 systolic ejection murmur heard best at the left lower sternal border. Otherwise regular rate and rhythm.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Elizabeth Scott is a 53-year-old female today who presents for evaluation of chest pain.
- Chest Pain: Unstable angina. Referral to cardiology recommended today for further evaluation and management. Prescribed aspirin daily and nitroglycerin as needed for chest pain.
- Diabetes Mellitus Type 2: Continue eye ophthalmology appointment for diabetic retinopathy screening today. Continue metformin 500 mg twice daily as prescribed. Order another hemoglobin A1c today and schedule follow-up in two weeks to review results and discuss any necessary adjustments to treatment plan.
- Hypertension: Trending high blood pressure noted on chart review today. Prescribed hydrochlorothiazide as needed for hypertension management at home with blood pressure monitoring via home blood pressure cuff at Epic MyChart portal daily in the morning upon waking until next clinic visit in two weeks when we will review findings together with additional recommendations if necessary.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Left knee pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Angela Powell is a pleasant 81-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of left knee pain. The onset of her symptoms began approximately 1 week ago when she was running with her niece and fell, twisting her knee in some kind of funky way. She states that she heard a pop at the time. She denies any loss of sensation or weakness in the left leg. She rates her pain as a 4 out of 10, which has been worsening. She reports that she has been limping ever since and it has not gotten better. She had an ulcer not too long ago and was told by her doctor that she cannot take Advil or ibuprofen due to this. She has been taking Tylenol for pain, but states that it only helps for a short period of time before the pain returns.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports left knee pain.
Neurological: Denies any numbness or weakness.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Musculoskeletal: Examination of the left knee reveals edema and effusion. There is moderate range of motion with pain on flexion and extension. Negative Lachman's test and negative valgus/varus tests.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-rays of the left knee were obtained today and are unremarkable.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Angela Powell is an 81-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for evaluation of left knee pain.

Medical Reasoning:
- The patient sustained an injury to her left knee when she was running with her niece and fell, twisting her knee in some kind of funky way.
- She rates her pain as a 4 out of 10, which has been worsening.
- She denies any loss of sensation or weakness in the left leg.
- X-rays were obtained today and are unremarkable.
- I believe this is a medial collateral ligament strain based on examination findings.
- Medical Treatment:
- I have prescribed tramadol 50 mg twice daily for pain management.
- I have recommended that she wear a knee immobilizer for the next week to keep the knee from moving so it can heal a little bit and reduce some inflammation.
- I have recommended that she ice it three or four times per day for twenty minutes at a time to help reduce swelling.
- We discussed that she should avoid running with her niece for the next three weeks while we allow time for healing.

Abnormal lab findings.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Joyce Price is a 50-year-old female who presents for follow-up to an abnormal lab finding. She reports that she has been feeling really tired lately over the past couple of months. She used to be very active, running and climbing, but over the past month, she has noticed that her energy has really gone down. She has been so tired and exhausted and has not been able to keep up with her exercise routine. She denies any blood in her stools or dark stools. She denies spotting with her periods. She denies chest pain, shortness of breath, fever, chills, or body aches. She does note some weight loss but notes that this is due to her increased exercise.

She reports that she stopped smoking several years ago but still has emphysema changes on her chest x-ray. Her breathing is currently okay but gets a little bit harder during the changes of season due to allergies.

Regarding congestive heart failure, she reports that she is watching her diet and staying away from salty foods.

She notes that she does have a good support system with her boyfriend and brother.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Cardiovascular: Grade 2/6 systolic ejection murmur heard at the left lower sternal border.
Respiratory: Lungs are clear bilaterally.

note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Hemoglobin level is 8.2.
Anemia labs are pending.
note.assessment_and_plan:

Abnormal lab findings.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's hemoglobin level is low at 8.2 which is below normal levels of 13-14 g/dL.

- Patient Education and Counseling: I advised the patient on lifestyle modifications including smoking cessation and dietary modifications such as limiting salt intake.
Next Steps: We will follow up in 1 week for further evaluation.

Annual exam.

Evelyn Morris is a 56-year-old female with a past medical history significant for coronary artery disease, prior carpal tunnel release, and a herniated disc who presents for her annual exam.

The patient reports that she has been doing well over the last year. She notes that her herniated disc in her back has been doing well. She has not had any back pain or limitations in movement. She is back to work and has full range of motion in her hands. She denies any numbness or tingling in her hands.

Regarding her carpal tunnel issues, she had that fixed a couple of years ago. She reports that she is good and back to work. She denies any recurrent issues.

The patient reports that she has had prior stenting in the past for her heart vessels. Over the last month, she has been experiencing chest pain but denies shortness of breath, nausea, or vomiting. The chest pain occurs when she walks and resolves with rest.

She endorses nasal congestion from allergies due to pollen.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Cardiovascular: Endorses chest pressure.
Neurological: Endorses numbness and tingling in the hands.
Musculoskeletal: Endorses lower extremity edema, muscle aches.

Annual exam.

Upper respiratory infection.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Logan Harris is a 57-year-old male who presents today for evaluation of an upper respiratory infection.

The patient reports that about a week ago he started to get a cold. In the last 2-3 days, it seemed to move into his chest. He has had some post nasal drip for the beginning of the week, but it has left his head and gone right down to his upper chest. He denies any sinus pain or post nasal drip. The patient reports that he has been vaccinated against COVID-19 and has received both doses. He denies anyone else in his household being sick. The patient denies fevers, shortness of breath, or chest pain.

The patient reports that he has been doing well with diet but acknowledges that there was some travel over the last week or so which may have impacted his diet. He is currently taking Crestor 20 mg daily and tolerates it well without any muscle aches.

The patient reports that he had coronary artery bypass grafting last year and is doing well with no chest pain. He continues to exercise regularly.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Reports fever.
• Respiratory: Reports congestion in the chest.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

• Head and Neck: Lymphadenopathy of the cervical region.
• Respiratory: Bilateral ronchi and wheezing.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Lipid panel: Within normal limits.
COVID-19 test: Positive.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Logan Harris is a 57-year-old male who presents today for evaluation of an upper respiratory infection.

Medical Reasoning:
The patient presents today for evaluation of an upper respiratory infection. His symptoms are consistent with this diagnosis, however, given his positive COVID-19 test, I believe this is likely due to COVID-19 as opposed to a viral upper respiratory tract infection. His oxygen saturation was within normal limits on examination today which supports this diagnosis as well. I discussed this with him today and advised him to quarantine for 10 days while avoiding contact with other household members as well as take off work until symptoms improve.
Regarding his high cholesterol, we discussed dietary modifications and continued Crestor 20 mg daily as tolerated. We will follow up in 6 months at which time we will order another lipid panel.
Regarding his coronary artery bypass grafting, I advised him that his coronary artery disease seems under control at this time based on his current symptoms and exercise tolerance without chest pain. We will follow up in 6 months at which time we will order a stress test.

note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

The patient is a 75-year-old female who presents for a follow-up visit today.

Medical Reasoning:
The patient’s hemoglobin A1C was 9.9% last time we saw her. We discussed the importance of increasing her glimepiride dosage from 2 mg twice daily to 4 mg twice daily in order to better control her sugars. The patient has been compliant with this recommendation and will continue taking the current dosage of glimepiride at home until she receives the new prescription from me today. We discussed the importance of eating healthier and reducing carbohydrate intake as well as avoiding sugary beverages such as soda and juice. The patient reports that she has not had any pasta or bread in the house recently and that she prefers seltzer water over regular water.
Regarding her high blood pressure, we discussed rechecking it today as the numbers at home have improved since our last visit. The patient is currently on lisinopril/hydrochlorothiazide 20/25 mg once daily and metoprolol 50 mg once daily; however, we will continue these medications as prescribed today.
Regarding her hyperlipidemia and peripheral vascular disease with neuropathy, we discussed continuing atorvastatin at high dose to protect the arteries as recommended by Lipitor® (atorvastatin) tablets (10 mg) once daily until further notice due to the multiple medications she is already taking for other conditions including diabetes mellitus type II and hypertension.
The patient continues to smoke despite our previous discussion regarding smoking cessation; however, we will leave everything else the same for now until we can discuss smoking cessation again in detail later in the visit.
Regarding her vision improvement post-cataract surgery, I advised her that there may be an option for laser cleaning up the eye if needed in order to improve vision further.
The patient’s last eye exam was performed by Dr. Sanchez at Liberty Road Optometry approximately 1 year ago with new glasses obtained from them today.
The patient’s extremities are without edema; pulses are palpable on dorsalis pedis posterior tibial; mildly dry skin without skin breakdown; mildly decreased sensation in tips of first and second toes; thickened nails.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Evaluation of numbness and tingling.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Elijah Cook is a 60-year-old male who presents today for evaluation of numbness and tingling in his hands. The onset of these symptoms began several weeks ago, after he sustained a motor vehicle accident in December 2019 resulting in broken wrists. He states that the numbness and tingling have been worse since then, but they have gotten progressively worse over the last month. He notes that his right wrist was more severely injured than his left wrist at the time of the accident. He also reports mild stiffness in his neck, which he attributes to a contusion from the accident.

The patient reports that he has been wearing a splint on his right wrist only, but he wears it on his left sometimes. The patient notes that both wrists are now worse than they were prior to the injury. The patient denies any loss of sensation in his hands or fingers.

The patient reports that he is currently taking Coreg for hypertension and Lexapro for anxiety. He had prediabetes, but has since gotten it under control via dietary changes.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Constitutional: Fatigue, weight gain.
GI: Excessive appetite and bloating.
Eyes: Floaters.
Cardiovascular: Shortness of breath and leg swelling.
Endocrine: Always hungry.
Skin: Nail bed changes, dryness, itching.
Musculoskeletal: Gout and muscle pain.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Neurological Examination:
- Sensation: Normal except for diminished pinprick sensation in third and fourth fingers on the right hand. Decreased sensation in fourth and fifth fingers on the left hand.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Elijah Cook is a 60-year-old male who presents today for evaluation of numbness and tingling in both hands. Bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome is suspected based on his symptom presentation as well as examination findings today. We will schedule an EMG/nerve conduction study to further evaluate this possibility. After these studies are complete, he can return here for a follow-up visit if needed. If symptoms persist after these studies are completed, we can consider a referral to our hand clinic possibly for injections or carpal tunnel release surgery or refer him to an orthopedist for similar treatment options.

INSTRUCTIONS

Continue wearing splints.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Evaluation of bilateral hand numbness and tingling.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Kimberly Taylor is a 60-year-old right-handed female new patient referred by Dr. Jacob Ward for evaluation of bilateral hand numbness and tingling. The patient reports that she has had this numbness and tingling for a few weeks now. She states that the numbness and tingling are worse in her right hand, from her middle and ring finger all the way up to her forearm, and on her left, a bit more the pinky and the ring finger but not the middle. She denies pain, but states that they throb sometimes. She notes that she has been having some mild stiffness in her neck too. She hit her head during the accident, and they told her it was a contusion.

The patient reports that she is still wearing the splint only on her right wrist. She wears the left one also sometimes. The right one’s just worse. The splint seems to help both hands get better over time.

The patient denies any loss of sensation in her hands or fingers.

PAST HISTORY

Patient reports history of chronic kidney disease, prediabetes (diet controlled), hypertension, anxiety, GERD, diabetes, gout, history of MVA with broken wrists; contusion from hitting head during MVA.

CURRENT MEDICATIONS

Patient reports taking carvedilol 25 mg twice daily for hypertension and Lexapro 10 mg daily for anxiety.

ALLERGIES

Patient reports sulfa allergy.
note.objective_exam:

Question of bilateral cubital tunnel syndrome.

6 weeks status post right medial unicompartmental arthroplasty.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient is early in her recovery and will continue to improve. She should continue physical therapy to work on strength, range of motion, and endurance.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Abdominal pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Ashley James is a 14-year-old female who presents today for evaluation of abnormal renal ultrasound with an atrophic right kidney.

The patient was found to have a small kidney on one side. She reports that she was previously healthy, but now she is experiencing some stomach burning. She endorses hesitancy while urinating and states she has to wait for her urinary flow to commence. She endorses occasional dysuria. Ashley denies hematuria. Some beverages are associated with dysuria, thus the patient drinks mainly water, Gatorade and V8 juice.

The patient plays on softball team and is interested in joining a drill team over the summer.

PATIENT HISTORY

The patient's mother reports that the patient was found to have a small kidney on one side during an abdominal ultrasound performed 03/22/2021. The patient was treated for a stomach virus at that time and followed up with her primary care physician who recommended further testing. The patient then presented to Jackson Memorial Hospital where cysts were found on her kidney and ovaries, as well as swollen lymph nodes and infection. The patient was treated there and followed up with her primary care physician who recommended further testing.

The patient's mother also reports that the patient had three or four hospitalizations when she was four years old, sometimes for three days at a time. She believes this may have been due to an infection that affected her kidneys.

PATIENT'S FAMILIAR HISTORY

The patient's father had a kidney transplant which subsequently failed, died of dialysis in his 40s due to posterior urethral valves and obstructive neuropathy. He developed chronic kidney disease which was dialysis-dependent.

The patient's paternal great aunt also has end-stage renal disease which is dialysis dependent.

There is no family history of polycystic kidney disease.

CURRENT MEDICATIONS:
Pepcid 40 mg once daily.
Claritin as needed for allergies.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
- Neurological: Normal motor strength in all extremities without ataxia or dysmetria. No focal neurological deficits noted.
- Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm without murmurs, gallops or rubs.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Ashley James is a 14-year-old female who presents today for evaluation of abnormal renal ultrasound with an atrophic right kidney.
- Medical Reasoning: The findings from the abdominal ultrasound are consistent with an atrophic right kidney secondary to chronic renal disease. This may be contributing to left-sided hydronephrosis secondary to compensatory hypertrophy of the left kidney. There are no signs of active infection present today; however, she does endorse dysuria which may be related to her current medications or diet.
- Medical Treatment: We discussed treatment options today including dietary modifications, increased fluid intake, avoiding non-steroidal anti-inflammatory medicines like ibuprofen in favor of Tylenol, and continued medical treatment with Pepcid 40 mg once daily as well as Claritin as needed for allergies. We also discussed the importance of staying well-hydrated during physical activity such as softball in order to avoid dehydration which can put tremendous strain on her kidneys.
- Patient Education: I advised the parents that we will need to continue monitoring her renal function annually through ultrasounds and urinalysis in order to detect any changes early on so we can intervene if necessary. Additionally, we discussed the importance of maintaining a healthy diet and lifestyle in order to keep her kidneys healthy as an adult.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Left back pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Sean Phillips is a pleasant 35-year-old male who presents today for evaluation of left back pain. The patient reports that he had a lumbar microdiscectomy performed in 11/2020. Prior to the microdiscectomy, he was taking high-dose gabapentin for severe nerve pain through his back and lower extremities. He states that he has had left-sided low back pain since the surgery. The patient reports that his significant other always tells him to stretch and it always helps. He denies any physical activities that make his pain worse. He denies icing or taking any pain medications.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports left-sided low back pain.
Neurological: Reports left-sided lower extremity numbness and tingling.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

MSK: Examination of the lumbar spine reveals tenderness to palpation over the left paraspinal musculature.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-ray images of the lumbar spine were reviewed today and reveal no evidence of fracture or other abnormalities in the spine or vertebrae. Previous surgical site is visible and appears to have healed properly.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Sean Phillips is a pleasant 35-year-old male who presents today for evaluation of left-sided low back pain.

Medical Reasoning:
- The patient underwent a lumbar microdiscectomy in 11/2020, which resulted in left-sided low back pain.
- The patient has been taking high-dose gabapentin for severe nerve pain through his back and lower extremities prior to surgery.
- X-rays were reviewed today and reveal no evidence of fracture or other abnormalities in the spine or vertebrae. Previous surgical site is visible and appears to have healed properly.
- I believe this is due to a muscle pull from misalignment in his spine.
- Medical Treatment:
- Prescribed physical therapy at VA clinic for continued treatment.
- Prescribed meloxicam instead of ibuprofen due to high dose ibuprofen use, as we do not like to prescribe strong narcotics unless absolutely necessary.
- Prescribed demerol as well as referral to Pain Management Clinic for additional evaluation.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Sudden visual distortions and blurring of vision.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Emily White is a 77-year-old female who presents today for the evaluation of sudden visual distortions and blurring of vision. The patient reports that she has been having a decrease in vision when reading and straight lines. Her door frames have been looking crooked to her. She also reports that whenever she takes her husband out to a nice restaurant, she has trouble adjusting to those dim lights. She denies any history of macular degeneration.

The patient reports that she smokes approximately 1 pack of cigarettes per day.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Visual: Decreased vision when reading and straight lines.
• Neurological: Trouble adjusting to dim lights.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Eyes: Anterior segment examination reveals posterior chamber intraocular lenses in both eyes. The cornea is clear without media opacities, no microaneurysms, ciliochoroidal folds, or PCIs. Cup-to-disc ratio is 2 in the right eye and 3 in the left eye. Fundus examination of the right eye shows the retina to be attached without any tears or holes or pigment epithelium changes in the fovea. Posterior segment exam shows drusen in the macula, thickening of the retina, presence of subretinal fluid and exudates accumulation, positive for hemorrhage. Left eye: The cornea is clear without media opacities, no microaneurysms, ciliochoroidal folds, or PCIs. No pigment epithelium changes in the fovea; no hemorrhage or subretinal fluid; retina is attached.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Optical coherence tomography shows drusen deposit. Retinal pigment epithelium with subretinal fluid accumulation. The choroidal neovascular membrane can be visualized.
Fluorescein angiography reveals focal areas of leakage in the right eye consistent with neovascular age-related macular degeneration.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Neovascular age-related macular degeneration.
Medical Reasoning: The patient's symptoms are consistent with neovascular age-related macular degeneration as evidenced by her recent diagnostic testing which revealed focal areas of leakage in her right eye consistent with neovascular age-related macular degeneration.
Medical Treatment Plan: I have reviewed the results of her diagnostic tests and physical exam today today which are indicative of neovascular age-related macular degeneration at this stage it usually leads to more severe vision loss as abnormal blood vessels start to grow beneath the retina and they will leak fluid and blood creating a large blind spot in the center of visual field which is usually caused by smoking cigarettes which is why I recommended that she stop smoking cigarettes today as well as keep up with her blood pressure check regularly as well as keep a log for that purpose.
Patient Education Plan: I advised her that this disease may progress despite treatment but injections may slow down rate of vision decline or stop further vision loss but however it may also progress despite treatment do not hesitate to contact me if you have any questions.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Right ankle pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Jacqueline Price is a pleasant 28-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right ankle pain. The onset of her symptoms began after she fell off her mountain bike while mountain biking. She states that she heard a pop in her right ankle at the time of the injury. She denies any numbness or tingling in her toes. She reports that she has been taking Tylenol for pain, but it has not helped. She denies any fever, chills, or other constitutional symptoms.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Right ankle pain.
Neurological: Numbness and tingling in the heart.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Respiratory: No evidence of respiratory distress.
Cardiovascular: No murmurs, gallops, or rubs heard. No edema in the extremities.
Musculoskeletal: Examination of the right ankle reveals edema and erythema on the lateral malleolus on the right hand side. There is associated ecchymosis and a few excoriations. There is pain to palpation of the right lateral malleolus. There is decreased flexion and extension of the right ankle as well as internal and external rotation. There is no apparent injury to the knee or foot.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-ray of the right foot was obtained today and reviewed by me today. The radiographic findings are consistent with no acute fracture or bony abnormality.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

The patient presents today for evaluation of right ankle pain.
I do believe she has an acute right ankle sprain.
We will place her in an air cast and prescribe meloxicam 15 mg once daily.
I recommend ice therapy for 20 minutes 5 times a day.
I recommend weight-bearing as tolerated.
I anticipate that she will start feeling better in 2 weeks if she does not improve at that point we will consider physical therapy or further imaging.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Myocardial infarction.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Betty Garcia is a 72-year-old male who presents today for follow-up after a myocardial infarction. The patient reports that he was in the hospital for approximately 48 hours and has been home for the past 2 weeks. He states that he has been doing well since being discharged, but notes that he is still struggling and feels scared. The patient denies any chest pain since his stent placement.

The patient reports that he had a cardiac catheterization and wrist surgery. He states that his wrist is healing well and there is no infection.

The patient reports shortness of breath when walking around or moving anything.

The patient reports that he takes Brilinta twice a day every 12 hours, aspirin at night, Crestor 40 mg once a day, and Toprol 50 mg once a day.

The patient denies any issues with cost with Brilinta.

The patient states that he enjoys swimming but has not been able to do so due to his recent heart attack. He would like to resume swimming but wants to start slow.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Cardiovascular: Endorse chest pain.
Neurological: Endorse shortness of breath.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Neck: No jugular venous distention.
Cardiovascular: Grade 3/6 systolic ejection murmur heard at the left base. Otherwise, no murmurs, gallops, or rubs were appreciated. No carotid bruits were appreciated.
Respiratory: Lungs are clear bilaterally to auscultation.
Musculoskeletal: Right radial artery cardiac cath site is clean dry and intact. There is no hematoma. Palpable radial pulse.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Myocardial infarction.
- Continue aspirin lifelong until further advised.
- Continue Brilinta twice daily every 12 hours for at least one year until further advised.
- Continue Crestor 40 mg once daily lifelong until further advised.
- Order echocardiogram in 6 months for repeat evaluation of mild mitral regurgitation which was noted on echocardiogram today as well as mild left ventricular systolic dysfunction which was noted on echocardiogram today as well (ejection fraction approximately 50%).
- Refer to cardiac rehabilitation for increased confidence in exercise tolerance and dietary education/counseling due to mild left ventricular systolic dysfunction which was noted on echocardiogram today as well as mild mitral regurgitation which was noted on echocardiogram today as well (ejection fraction approximately 50%).
- Continue Toprol XL 50 mg once daily lifelong until further advised due to mild left ventricular systolic dysfunction which was noted on echocardiogram today as well as mild mitral regurgitation which was noted on echocardiogram today as well (ejection fraction approximately 50%).
- Order liver function studies and lipid panel to follow up with next time we meet.

Left shoulder pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Betty Rogers is a 50-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for left shoulder pain. The onset of her pain began 3 weeks ago and she denies any associated trauma. She is very active and has been renovating her basement recently. She denies any previous history of left shoulder pain.

Pain is constant and worsens with any pressure, such as when she sleeps at night. She cannot lay on her left side at all due to the pain. She also experiences pain when she sleeps directly on it, but the pain goes up into her neck. She rates her pain as a 7 without Tylenol and a 2-3 with Tylenol.

The patient reports that she has been taking Tylenol Extra Strength, 2 tablets every 6 to 8 hours.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports left shoulder pain.
Neurological: Denies numbness or tingling in the left arm or hand.
note.objective_exam:

Neurological: Examination of the left upper extremity reveals brisk capillary refill in less than 3 seconds bilaterally. Motor strength is intact to light touch bilaterally. Sensation is intact to light touch bilaterally.

note.objective_results:
RESULTS

note.assessment_and_plan:

Left shoulder pain.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's symptoms are most likely due to rotator cuff tendinopathy.

- Patient Education/ Counseling: I have discussed my findings with the patient today and advised her that many patients are successful with physical therapy so we will start with that take a conservative approach and see how she does after that time period if needed we can consider a steroid injection of that left shoulder which could hopefully get her some relief.
Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with my recommended medical treatment plan.

Right knee pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Matthew Allen is a pleasant 40-year-old male who presents today for evaluation of right knee pain. The patient reports that he was playing basketball yesterday and when he went up for a rebound, he came down and felt like his knee just popped. He states that the pain started swelling and he could hardly walk when it happened. The patient denies any history of prior right knee injuries. He states that he has been playing basketball for the first time in 2 years. He denies watching the game last night.

The patient reports that his blood pressure was 140/80 today. He states that this is a little bit high but he knows they recommended that he get a blood pressure cuff at home to check his blood pressure more often. He usually checks his blood pressure in the 140-150/80 range.

Regarding his diabetes, the patient reports that he is currently taking metformin 500 mg daily but skips taking it sometimes because it upsets his stomach. His A1C was 7.2 today.

The patient denies any dietary changes since the pandemic and states that he eats anything he wants.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Respiratory: Lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Cardiovascular: Grade 2 systolic ejection murmur heard best at left sternal border, no thrill, no radiation, no murmurs or gallops heard elsewhere.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-ray of Matthew Allen's right knee was reviewed today and revealed no fractures or bony abnormalities.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Right knee pain.
• Medical Reasoning: Matthew Allen sustained an MCL strain due to playing basketball yesterday.
• Medical Treatment Plan: I have prescribed Tylenol for pain management as well as Meloxicam fifteen milligrams for pain and swelling management. I have also placed him in a knee immobilizer to keep him off of the right leg for the next couple of weeks until we can obtain an MRI to further evaluate his right knee. We will follow up with an orthopedic specialist for further evaluation.
• Patient Education: I advised him to continue taking Tylenol for pain management as well as follow up with nutritionist to improve diet and lifestyle modifications.
• Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with recommended medical treatment plan.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Elevated and fluctuating blood pressure.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Robert Harris is a 67-year-old male with a history of essential hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and osteoarthritis who is here today with elevated and fluctuating blood pressures. The patient reports that his blood pressure has been well controlled over the last 3 to 4 weeks. However, he has experienced periods where he felt lightheaded and had a slight headache. When he checked his blood pressure, the upper number was occasionally over 180 mm Hg, which is higher than what he has seen in the past.

The patient denies passing out or chest pain. He does report some heaviness in his chest when his blood pressure is elevated. He denies any respiratory or breathing difficulty. The patient also reports occasional dizziness and a slight headache when his blood pressure numbers are higher.

The patient denies any fever, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, palpitations or heart racing.

The patient continues to take lisinopril 20 mg twice per day. He states that he has been using the pill box to keep track of his medication schedule but finds the app confusing and has not been using it consistently.

SOCIAL HISTORY

The patient enjoys playing golf.

MEDICATIONS

Lisinopril 20 mg twice per day; Atorvastatin; Occasional Tylenol.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Cardiovascular: Grade 3/6 systolic ejection murmur unchanged from prior exam. No murmurs from valves.
Respiratory: Mild bibasilar rales without wheezes or rhonchi. Excellent air movement bilaterally.
Musculoskeletal: Trace lower extremity edema bilaterally.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Elevated Blood Pressure.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's blood pressure is out of control at this time as evidenced by periods where it was elevated to over 180 mm Hg on multiple occasions. Additionally, he reports lightheadedness at times which may be related to hypotension secondary to elevated blood pressure.
- Medical Treatment: I have increased lisinopril to 60 mg twice daily and added hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily for additional BP control. I have recommended that the patient check his BP measurements twice daily for the next two weeks then we will follow up in two weeks at that time we will reassess how well these changes are working for him.
- Patient Education: I advised him that it is important to stay well hydrated especially when it warms up as we will be sweating more and losing more fluid through respiration.
- Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with these recommendations.
Hyperlipidemia.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's cholesterol levels were last checked approximately one month ago at which time they were within normal limits. However, he continues to experience elevated LDL cholesterol levels despite being on atorvastatin therapy alone. Additionally, there was an increase in white blood cells on his most recent CBC with differential which may be related to hyperlipidemia as well as an increase in creatinine levels on his most recent comprehensive metabolic panel which may also be related to hyperlipidemia.
- Medical Treatment: We will repeat a cholesterol panel as well as a CBC with differential and comprehensive metabolic panel today along with urinalysis tomorrow morning for further evaluation of hyperlipidemia. We will continue current management with atorvastatin until further evaluation is completed.
Osteoarthritis of bilateral knees.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient continues to experience pain while walking full course but otherwise tolerates activity well overall without any significant limitations due to pain or disability from osteoarthritis of bilateral knees at this time.
- Medical Treatment: Continue current management with Tylenol for mild pain if needed while staying active as best you can do not overdo it but walking and golfing when you can.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Cough.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Billy Wright is a 74-year-old male who presents today for evaluation of a cough. The patient reports that his cough started about a week ago and has been productive of yellow sputum. He notes that he has been feeling worse over the last two days. The patient denies fevers, chills, shortness of breath, runny nose, sore throat, sinus pain or pressure. He does report congestion and drainage down his throat as well as sinus pressure.

The patient reports that he is a teacher and that he was sad to see the Cincinnati Bengals lose the Super Bowl today. He also reports that he twisted his right knee today while coughing and falling down the stairs. He states that he was able to walk this morning but notes that it hurts mostly on the inside of his knee. He denies limping but does report some ecchymosis to the right medial knee. The patient denies taking any pain medication.

The patient reports that he has had hypertension for several years and has been taking lisinopril 20 mg daily. He states that he does not check his blood pressure at home and denies taking any salt restriction into account with his lisinopril.

The patient also reports that he has type 2 diabetes mellitus which is currently being treated with metformin 1000 mg twice daily. He states that he does not take his blood sugars at home.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Reports fever.
• Respiratory: Reports productive cough with yellow sputum.
• Musculoskeletal: Reports right knee pain.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

• Head and Neck: Pain to palpation of bilateral maxillary sinuses on nasal exam. Erythema and edema of the nasal turbinates bilaterally with associated yellow discharge on throat exam. No erythema or edema or exudate in the peritonsillar space on neck examination. Bilateral cervical lymphadenopathy.
• Respiratory: Coarse rhonchi present bilaterally which clears with cough on lung exam.
• Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm without murmurs on cardiac exam.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Billy Wright is a 74-year-old male who presents today for evaluation of a cough.

Medical Reasoning:
I do believe this is just a viral syndrome at this time, likely causing some mild bronchitis. I recommend supportive care including over-the-counter medications such as guaifenesin six hundred milligrams twice daily to help him clear some phlegm from his lungs; however, I do not think antibiotics are indicated at this time due to lack of signs of bacterial infection such as fever or purulent sputum production. If symptoms worsen, we can consider ordering a chest x-ray to rule out pneumonia.

Medical Treatment:
I have prescribed guaifenesin six hundred milligrams twice daily for supportive care for your cough today.
I have recommended you continue lisinopril 20 mg daily for your hypertension today.
We will order a lipid panel to make sure everything is okay from that standpoint today as well.
We will order a hemoglobin A1c tomorrow to make sure we do not need to make any adjustments to your metformin today as well.
We will refer you to physical therapy tomorrow for strengthening exercises around your right knee due to your recent fall today which resulted in right medial collateral ligament strain from the fall this morning.
We will order an x-ray of your right knee tomorrow due to your recent fall this morning which resulted in right medial collateral ligament strain from the fall this morning as well as ecchymosis noted in the right medial knee today which may indicate some soft tissue injury or possible fracture despite my clinical suspicion being low given how recently it occurred today.
We will continue metformin 1000 mg twice daily for your diabetes mellitus today as well since you are currently doing well with it but we will monitor your sugar intake going forward through our patient portal so we can adjust if necessary.

- Patient understands and agrees with recommended medical treatment plan.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Vision changes.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Matthew Thomas is a pleasant 65-year-old male who presents today for evaluation of vision changes. The patient reports that he has been having trouble adjusting in the dark, especially when eating out at fancy restaurants. He notes that his vision has been decreased when reading, especially in dim environments. The patient also reports that when looking at straight lines, such as door frames, they look crooked to him. He denies any diplopia or floaters.

The patient reports that he and his wife have been eating out almost every night and that he has been having trouble adjusting in the dark environment. He notes that this has been getting worse over the last 3-4 months. The patient denies any history of trauma to his right eye.

The patient states that he was recently at a restaurant called Italiain and it reminded him of the movie Soprano's Family. He was very excited about going back there soon.

The patient reports that he has smoked 1 pack of cigarettes daily for the past and has tried hypnosis, lozenges, chewing gum, and nicotine patches to help him quit smoking but he continues to smoke.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Vision: Decreased vision when reading especially in dim environments.
• Neurological: Diplopia or double vision.
note.objective_exam:

Eyes: Anterior segment examination reveals posterior chamber intraocular lenses in both eyes for the right eye. The cornea is clear with no neovascularization or cup-to-disc ratio of.2. Fundus examination of the right eye shows the retina to be attached 360 degrees with no holes or tears noted and RPE changes in the fovea. The posterior segment exam shows drusen in the macula retinal thickening and presence of subretinal fluid and exudate accumulation and it is positive for a hemorrhage. For the left eye, the cornea is clear with no neovascularization or cup-to-disc ratio of.3. RPE changes in the fovea without hemorrhage noted or subretinal fluid noted and the retina is attached appropriately.

He was skiing with some friends and was going down in the snow when he could not see as the two paths came together. The front end of his skis dug into the snow and he ended up doing a cartwheel but stopped halfway through. He could feel a pop in his right knee and then immediately experienced pain in his right knee. He denies any previous knee injuries.

The patient reports that he has been able to walk a little bit but notes that it is swollen and painful. He has been icing his right knee off and on, as well as taking Advil for pain management.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports right knee pain.
Neurological: Denies any other injuries to other parts of his body.

CV: No murmurs, gallops, or rubs are appreciated.
Respiratory: No wheezes, rales, or rhonchi are appreciated.
Cardiovascular: No edema is appreciated.

note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Joe Reed is a pleasant 42-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for evaluation of right knee contusion.

Imaging studies were obtained today which revealed no fractures or bony abnormalities.
Medical Reasoning: This patient presents with a history of a right knee contusion after sustaining an injury while skiing over the weekend on Saturday. His examination today revealed edema and ecchymosis surrounding his joint, positive pain to palpation bilaterally, pain with flexion and extension bilaterally, full range of motion without tenderness to palpation, and no bony abnormalities on x-ray. These findings are consistent with a right knee contusion.
Medical Treatment Plan: I have advised him to rest his right knee, apply ice 2-3 times per day for 20 minutes at a time, take nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory medication such as ibuprofen every 6-8 hours as needed for pain management. I have also recommended that we follow up in 1 week if this does not improve.

Follow-up of nonsmall cell lung cancer.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Angela King is a 58-year-old female who presents today for follow-up of nonsmall cell lung cancer. She reports that she has been experiencing shortness of breath over the weekend. She had previously been very active, taking mile-long walks with her doberman. She notes that she can no longer walk down the street without being short of breath. She denies any cough or phlegm. She denies fever, body aches, sore throat, or sinus pain. She does report that every time she swallows it hurts and feels like food is getting stuck in her chest. The patient reports that she has been taking Ensure and liquids but has not been able to take in much hydrocortisone due to the pain.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Denies fever.
• Respiratory: Reports shortness of breath, dry cough, dysphagia.
• Cardiovascular: Denies chest pain.
• Musculoskeletal: Reports lower extremity edema.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Neck: No cervical lymphadenopathy or subclavicular adenopathy.
Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm without murmurs.
Respiratory: Crackles bilaterally.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Nonsmall cell lung cancer.
• Medical Reasoning: The patient presents today for follow-up of nonsmall cell lung cancer. Her most recent pathology report shows evidence of a 4.4 cm left upper lobe nodule and her chest x-ray obtained today was reviewed by me today and not yet reviewed.
• Medical Treatment Plan: We will continue her current neo-adjuvant chemotherapy regimen with cisplatin and etoposide as tolerated. We will also continue radiation therapy at 45 Gy in fractions as tolerated. When the regimen is complete we will perform additional testing to see if we can resect the tumor at this point it has gotten a little smaller. We will also discuss surgical options with her at that time.
Radiation pneumonitis.
• Medical Reasoning: The patient presents today for evaluation of radiation pneumonitis due to her recent radiation therapy to the lungs.
• Medical Treatment Plan: I have prescribed prednisone 40 mg daily for 5 days to help reduce inflammation in her lungs and improve her breathing. This should help with hydration while she is undergoing chemotherapy treatment as well.
Painful swallowing (odyophagia).
• Medical Reasoning: The patient presents today for evaluation of painful swallowing secondary to radiation pneumonitis due to inflammation in her lungs which has crept up into her esophagus causing dysphagia.
• Medical Treatment Plan: I have prescribed lidocaine squishy swallows for 4 times daily to help alleviate dysphagia while eating.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Kidney stone.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Joshua Reyes is a pleasant 18-year-old male who presents today for evaluation of right flank pain. The patient reports that he has been experiencing right flank pain for the last 2 weeks. He describes the pain radiating down to his groin. The patient states that the pain is under control but he experiences bouts where it gets a little out of control. He denies any urinary symptoms including hematuria, dysuria, or dyschezia. The patient reports that he has been taking ibuprofen for his pain but it persists.

The patient denies nausea, vomiting, or chills.

The patient reports that he has a personal history of kidney stones and some have passed independently while others required surgical intervention or lithotripsy. He also notes that all family members have had kidney stones in the past.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Denies fevers, chills, or weight loss.
• Musculoskeletal: Reports right flank pain radiating to groin.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

CVS: Tenderness to palpation in the right upper quadrant.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

CT scan of the right flank was reviewed today, 05/06/2022. It revealed a kidney stone measuring 0.5 cm in size, located on the proximal right ureter. There is no evidence of hydronephrosis.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Joshua Reyes is a pleasant 18-year-old male who presents today for evaluation of right flank pain.
• Medical Reasoning: This appears to be a new kidney stone based on his history and exam findings today.
• Medical Treatment: Continue ibuprofen as needed for pain management. I have prescribed tramadol 50 mg as needed for breakthrough pain today and will follow up with him in 1-2 weeks if he continues to experience symptoms at that time.
• Patient Education and Counseling: I advised him to continue drinking fluids and use a strainer when urinating to help pass the stone.

Shortness of breath.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Frank Lee is a 54-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for shortness of breath. The patient reports that he has been experiencing shortness of breath for about a week. He notes that this has been occurring more with walking quickly and stairs. He denies any shortness of breath when sleeping at night. The patient reports that he has had similar symptoms in the past, but they resolved after increasing his Lasix dose from 20 mg to 40 mg daily. He denies any swelling in his legs, but does report increased urination at night.

The patient reports that he is a basketball fan and watched the NBA playoffs last night.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Cardiovascular: Reports shortness of breath.
Musculoskeletal: Reports knee pain.
Neurological: Reports foot pain.

Neck: No jugular venous distension.
Respiratory: Bibasilar crackles with occasional rhonchi that clear with coughing.

Musculoskeletal: Bilateral pitting edema.

INSTRUCTIONS:

- Order uric acid level due to possible gout flare.
